## 📄 datasheet.js

/**
 * datasheet.js
 *
 * Generic Tabulator child-datasheet engine for Curator.
 * Called by _datasheet.html's <script type="module"> block on every
 * panel tab that includes a child datasheet (Tasks, Emails, Phones,
 * URLs, Contacts, etc.).
 *
 * Usage (from _datasheet.html's generated module script):
 *
 *   import { initDatasheet } from '/static/js/datasheet.js';
 *
 *   initDatasheet({
 *     containerId:  'tasks-datasheet',
 *     entity:       'tasks',
 *     queryName:    'for_project',
 *     queryParams:  '12',
 *     columns:      [...],
 *     parentField:  'project_id',   // explicit FK — never guessed
 *   });
 *
 * Save/delete routes live under /crew/{entity}/... (see
 * CHANGEDOC_DATASHEET_URL_AND_SUCCESS_FLAG_FIX.md). Save success is
 * read from body.success !== false (not HTTP status — the API returns
 * failures as HTTP 200 with a success:false envelope). Delete success
 * is a bare HTTP 204; failure is HTTP 200 with a success:false envelope.
 *
 * Known gap: + Add button wiring is deferred to the Tasks UI wiring
 * changedoc (see nested_master_detail_design.md) — Add for Tasks opens
 * the nested detail form, not an inline Tabulator row.
 */

export function initDatasheet(config) {
    const {
        containerId,
        entity,
        queryName,
        queryParams,
        columns,
        parentField,  // explicit parent FK field name — required for INSERT
                      // to include the correct parent id in the payload.
                      // Pass '' or omit if this datasheet has no parent FK.
    } = config;

    const container = document.getElementById(containerId);
    if (!container) return;

    const ajaxUrl = `/api/query/${entity}/${queryName}?params=${queryParams}`;

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Save a row to the server
    //
    // Error response contract (see projects.py save_new_project /
    // save_project): success = flat record at HTTP 200; failure =
    // {"success": false, "message": "...", "data": ...} ALSO at HTTP 200.
    // This means resp.ok is true in both cases — the only reliable success
    // check is body.success !== false. Matches detail-panel.js's saveForm();
    // keep both in sync if this contract ever changes.
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    async function saveRow(row) {
        const data = row.getData();
        const isNew = !data.id;

        // Don't save a new row with no content — just delete it
        const firstEditable = columns.find(c => c.editor);
        if (isNew && firstEditable && !data[firstEditable.field]) {
            row.delete();
            return true;
        }

        const url = isNew
            ? `/crew/${entity}/save`
            : `/crew/${entity}/${data.id}/save`;

        // Only send editable columns
        const editableFields = columns
            .filter(c => c.editor && c.field !== 'id')
            .map(c => c.field);

        const payload = {};
        editableFields.forEach(f => { payload[f] = data[f] ?? null; });

        // For new rows, include the parent FK with its explicit field name.
        // parentField replaces the old string-guessing heuristic that produced
        // task_id instead of project_id for the Tasks entity.
        if (isNew && parentField && queryParams) {
            payload[parentField] = queryParams;
        }

        let body;
        try {
            const resp = await fetch(url, {
                method: 'POST',
                headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify(payload),
            });
            body = await resp.json();
        } catch (err) {
            alert('Save error: ' + err.message);
            return false;
        }

        if (body.success === false) {
            alert(body.message || 'Save failed');
            return false;
        }

        row.update(body);
        return true;
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Delete a row from the server
    //
    // Error response contract (see projects.py delete_project): success =
    // bare HTTP 204, no body; failure = {"success": false, "message": "..."}
    // at HTTP 200. Unlike save, there's no body to check on success (204
    // has none) — so delete's check is on status code, not body.success.
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    async function deleteRow(row) {
        const id = row.getData().id;
        if (!id) { row.delete(); return; }

        if (!confirm('Delete this row?')) return;

        let resp;
        try {
            resp = await fetch(`/crew/${entity}/${id}`, { method: 'DELETE' });
        } catch (err) {
            alert('Delete error: ' + err.message);
            return;
        }

        if (resp.status === 204) {
            row.delete();
            return;
        }

        const body = await resp.json().catch(() => ({ message: resp.statusText }));
        alert(body.message || 'Delete failed');
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Tabulator init — uses global Tabulator loaded by base.html via CDN
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    const table = new Tabulator(container, {  // eslint-disable-line no-undef
        height: '100%',
        layout: 'fitColumns',
        ajaxURL: ajaxUrl,
        ajaxConfig: { headers: { 'Accept': 'application/json' } },
        ajaxResponse: (url, params, response) => response.records || [],
        editTriggerEvent: 'dblclick',
        columns: columns,

        cellEdited: async function(cell) {
            await saveRow(cell.getRow());
        },

        rowContextMenu: [
            {
                label: 'Delete row',
                action: (e, row) => deleteRow(row),
            }
        ],

        dataLoadError: (error) => {
            console.error(`Failed to load ${entity}/${queryName}:`, error);
        },
    });

    // Escape — delete empty new row, or cancel edit
    document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
        if (e.key === 'Escape') {
            const newRow = table.getRows().find(r => !r.getData().id);
            if (newRow) newRow.delete();
        }
    });

    // Store reference on window for parent access (e.g. refresh after save)
    window[`tabulator_${containerId}`] = table;
    window[`refresh_${containerId}`]   = () => table.setData(ajaxUrl);
}

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_DATASHEET_URL_AND_SUCCESS_FLAG_FIX

# CHANGEDOC — Datasheet Save/Delete URLs + Success-Flag Bug Fix

**Status:** Ready to apply — Python/JS only, no SQL, no pgAdmin step.

## Summary

Three fixes, one changedoc, because they share a root cause (wrong
assumption about how failure is signaled by the API):

1. `datasheet.js` — save/delete URLs point at `/api/{entity}/...`,
   which doesn't exist. Real routes are `/crew/{entity}/...`.
2. `datasheet.js` — `saveRow()` checks `resp.ok` (HTTP status) to decide
   success/failure. The actual API contract returns failures as HTTP
   200 with `{"success": false, "message": "...", "data": ...}` in the
   body (confirmed in `projects.py`'s `save_new_project`/`save_project`
   routes). `resp.ok` is always `true` for these responses, so a
   rejected save (duplicate name, validation failure, etc.) would be
   silently treated as successful.
3. `detail-panel.js` — same bug, already shipped. `saveForm()` checks
   `res.ok` instead of `body.success`. This is a **found latent bug in
   already-shipped code**, not a new gap — flagging per project rules
   rather than fixing without a paper trail.

Delete is different: `delete_project` returns bare HTTP 204 (no body)
on success, and `{"success": false, "message": "..."}` at HTTP 200 on
failure. So delete's fix is a status-code check (204 vs. everything
else), not a body-parsing check — `resp.ok` alone would incorrectly
treat a 200-with-failure delete response as success.

---

## File 1 — `static/js/datasheet.js`

### BEFORE

```javascript
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Save a row to the server
    // NOTE: URLs below (/api/{entity}/...) do not exist in the current app —
    // real routes are /crew/{entity}/... This is a known gap, not addressed
    // in this changedoc. Saving will 404 until the URL fix lands.
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    async function saveRow(row) {
        const data = row.getData();
        const isNew = !data.id;

        // Don't save a new row with no content — just delete it
        const firstEditable = columns.find(c => c.editor);
        if (isNew && firstEditable && !data[firstEditable.field]) {
            row.delete();
            return true;
        }

        const url = isNew
            ? `/api/${entity}/save`
            : `/api/${entity}/${data.id}/save`;

        // Only send editable columns
        const editableFields = columns
            .filter(c => c.editor && c.field !== 'id')
            .map(c => c.field);

        const payload = {};
        editableFields.forEach(f => { payload[f] = data[f] ?? null; });

        // For new rows, include the parent FK with its explicit field name.
        // parentField replaces the old string-guessing heuristic that produced
        // task_id instead of project_id for the Tasks entity.
        if (isNew && parentField && queryParams) {
            payload[parentField] = queryParams;
        }

        const resp = await fetch(url, {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
            body: JSON.stringify(payload),
        });

        if (!resp.ok) {
            const err = await resp.json().catch(() => ({ detail: resp.statusText }));
            alert(err.detail || 'Save failed');
            return false;
        }

        const saved = await resp.json();
        row.update(saved);
        return true;

    // NOTE: Same URL gap as saveRow above.

        if (!id) { row.delete(); return; }

        if (!confirm('Delete this row?')) return;

        const resp = await fetch(`/api/${entity}/${id}`, { method: 'DELETE' });
        if (resp.ok) {
            row.delete();
        } else {
            alert('Delete failed');

```

### AFTER

```javascript
    // check is body.success !== false. Matches detail-panel.js's corrected

            .filter(c => c.editor && c.field !== 'id')

    //

```

### Why

- `/api/{entity}/...` never existed as a route — every real save/delete
  route lives under `/crew/{entity}/...` (confirmed directly against
  `projects.py`). Saves and deletes were 404ing silently before this fix.
- The API's actual failure contract (HTTP 200 + `success: false`) means
  `resp.ok` can't distinguish success from failure for saves — it's
  `true` either way. Checking `body.success === false` explicitly is the
  only correct check, and matches what your project memory documents as
  the intended contract.
- Delete is asymmetric: success is bare 204 (no JSON body to parse),
  failure is 200 with a body. The check has to branch on status code
  first, not attempt `resp.json()` unconditionally (which would throw
  on the empty 204 body).
- Wrapped both in `try/catch` for network failures (server unreachable,
  connection dropped) — previously unhandled, would have thrown an
  uncaught promise rejection instead of a user-visible alert.

## File 2 — `static/js/detail-panel.js`

### BEFORE

```javascript
async function saveForm() {
  const form = getForm();
  if (!form) return null;

  const entity   = form.dataset.entity;
  const recordId = form.dataset.id;
  const isNew    = !recordId;

  const formData = new FormData(form);
  const data     = Object.fromEntries(formData);

  const url = isNew
    ? `/crew/${entity}/save`
    : `/crew/${entity}/${recordId}/save`;

  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(data),
    });

    if (res.ok) {
      const saved = await res.json();
      // Update form id to the newly saved record's id
      form.dataset.id = saved.id;
      const panel = getPanel();
      if (panel) panel.dataset.id = saved.id;
      return saved;
    } else {
      // crew.py returns {"success": false, "message": "..."} on proc
      // rejection (duplicate name, not found, etc.) — read message, not
      // detail, or this always falls back to the generic string below.
      const err = await res.json().catch(() => ({ message: res.statusText }));
      alert(err.message || 'Save failed');
      return null;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Save error:', err);
    alert('Save error: ' + err.message);
    return null;
  }
}
```

### AFTER

```javascript
async function saveForm() {
  const form = getForm();
  if (!form) return null;

  const entity   = form.dataset.entity;
  const recordId = form.dataset.id;
  const isNew    = !recordId;

  const formData = new FormData(form);
  const data     = Object.fromEntries(formData);

  const url = isNew
    ? `/crew/${entity}/save`
    : `/crew/${entity}/${recordId}/save`;

  try {
    const res  = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(data),
    });
    const body = await res.json();

    // FOUND BUG (fixed here): this used to check res.ok, but crew.py's
    // proc-backed save routes return failures as {"success": false,
    // "message": "...", "data": ...} at HTTP 200 — not a non-2xx status.
    // res.ok was always true, so a rejected save (duplicate name, etc.)
    // was silently treated as successful: form.dataset.id got set to
    // undefined (saved.id on a failure body), and the caller proceeded
    // as if the record had saved. The only reliable check is
    // body.success !== false, matching datasheet.js's saveRow().
    if (body.success === false) {
      alert(body.message || 'Save failed');
      return null;
    }

    // Update form id to the newly saved record's id
    form.dataset.id = body.id;
    const panel = getPanel();
    if (panel) panel.dataset.id = body.id;
    return body;
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Save error:', err);
    alert('Save error: ' + err.message);
    return null;
  }
}
```

### Why

- **This is a found bug in already-shipped code**, not part of the
  datasheet URL fix — flagged explicitly per "never silently fix
  problems." Before this fix, a rejected save (e.g. duplicate project
  name) was silently accepted by the UI: `res.ok` is `true` for a 200
  response regardless of body content, so the `if (res.ok)` branch ran,
  `saved.id` was `undefined` (since the failure body has no `id` key),
  and the form/panel were left thinking a save succeeded when it hadn't.
- Fix mirrors `datasheet.js`'s corrected `saveRow()` exactly — same
  contract, same check, so both files can never drift back into
  disagreement about how to read a save response.

---

## Not in scope for this changedoc

- `+ Add Task` button wiring — deferred to the Tasks UI wiring
  changedoc, now that the nested master-detail design doc
  (`nested_master_detail_design.md`) has settled what "Add" actually
  does for Tasks (opens the nested detail form, not an inline Tabulator
  row).
- `add_url` / `data-add-url` on `_datasheet_with_header.html` — left
  as-is for now; whether it's still needed depends on how the Tasks tab
  wiring changedoc wires `+ Add Task` to the nested form. Revisit then.
- Any other entity's save/delete routes beyond what's already confirmed
  in `projects.py` — assumed consistent (task/contact/organization
  routes should follow the same `call_proc_and_refetch` /
  `delete_via_proc` helper pattern in `deps.py`), but not individually
  re-verified here.

## Testing notes

- No existing test file covers `datasheet.js` or `detail-panel.js`
  directly (these are browser JS, not part of the pytest suite).
  Manual verification: open a Project's Tasks tab (once wired), edit a
  task inline, confirm it round-trips through `/crew/tasks/{id}/save`
  and shows updated values without a page reload. Try a save that
  should be rejected by the proc (e.g. blank required field, once
  validation exists) and confirm the alert fires instead of a false
  "success."

```javascript
    : `/crew/${entity}/${recordId}/save`;

    const res = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(data),
    });

    if (res.ok) {
      const saved = await res.json();
      // Update form id to the newly saved record's id
      form.dataset.id = saved.id;
      const panel = getPanel();
      if (panel) panel.dataset.id = saved.id;
      return saved;
    } else {
      // crew.py returns {"success": false, "message": "..."} on proc
      // rejection (duplicate name, not found, etc.) — read message, not
      // detail, or this always falls back to the generic string below.
      const err = await res.json().catch(() => ({ message: res.statusText }));
      alert(err.message || 'Save failed');
      return null;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Save error:', err);
    alert('Save error: ' + err.message);
    return null;
  }
}
```

### AFTER

```javascript
async function saveForm() {
  const form = getForm();
  if (!form) return null;

  const entity   = form.dataset.entity;
  const recordId = form.dataset.id;
  const isNew    = !recordId;

  const formData = new FormData(form);
  const data     = Object.fromEntries(formData);

  const url = isNew
    ? `/crew/${entity}/save`
    : `/crew/${entity}/${recordId}/save`;

  try {
    const res  = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(data),
    });
    const body = await res.json();

    // FOUND BUG (fixed here): this used to check res.ok, but crew.py's
    // proc-backed save routes return failures as {"success": false,
    // "message": "...", "data": ...} at HTTP 200 — not a non-2xx status.
    // res.ok was always true, so a rejected save (duplicate name, etc.)
    // was silently treated as successful: form.dataset.id got set to
    // undefined (saved.id on a failure body), and the caller proceeded
    // as if the record had saved. The only reliable check is
    // body.success !== false, matching datasheet.js's saveRow().
    if (body.success === false) {
      alert(body.message || 'Save failed');
      return null;
    }

    // Update form id to the newly saved record's id
    form.dataset.id = body.id;
    const panel = getPanel();
    if (panel) panel.dataset.id = body.id;
    return body;
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Save error:', err);
    alert('Save error: ' + err.message);
    return null;
  }
}
```

### Why

- **This is a found bug in already-shipped code**, not part of the
  datasheet URL fix — flagged explicitly per "never silently fix
  problems." Before this fix, a rejected save (e.g. duplicate project
  name) was silently accepted by the UI: `res.ok` is `true` for a 200
  response regardless of body content, so the `if (res.ok)` branch ran,
  `saved.id` was `undefined` (since the failure body has no `id` key),
  and the form/panel were left thinking a save succeeded when it hadn't.
- Fix mirrors `datasheet.js`'s corrected `saveRow()` exactly — same
  contract, same check, so both files can never drift back into
  disagreement about how to read a save response.

---

## Not in scope for this changedoc

- `+ Add Task` button wiring — deferred to the Tasks UI wiring
  changedoc, now that the nested master-detail design doc
  (`nested_master_detail_design.md`) has settled what "Add" actually
  does for Tasks (opens the nested detail form, not an inline Tabulator
  row).
- `add_url` / `data-add-url` on `_datasheet_with_header.html` — left
  as-is for now; whether it's still needed depends on how the Tasks tab
  wiring changedoc wires `+ Add Task` to the nested form. Revisit then.
- Any other entity's save/delete routes beyond what's already confirmed
  in `projects.py` — assumed consistent (task/contact/organization
  routes should follow the same `call_proc_and_refetch` /
  `delete_via_proc` helper pattern in `deps.py`), but not individually
  re-verified here.

## Testing notes

- No existing test file covers `datasheet.js` or `detail-panel.js`
  directly (these are browser JS, not part of the pytest suite).
  Manual verification: open a Project's Tasks tab (once wired), edit a
  task inline, confirm it round-trips through `/crew/tasks/{id}/save`
  and shows updated values without a page reload. Try a save that
  should be rejected by the proc (e.g. blank required field, once
  validation exists) and confirm the alert fires instead of a false
  "success."

## 📄 nested_master_detail_design

# Nested Master-Detail Pattern — Design Doc

**Status:** Agreed design, not yet implemented.
**Scope:** Applies to Tasks tab first. Subtasks (recursive nesting) deferred — see "Deferred" below.

---

## Problem

Child datasheet tabs (Tasks, Emails, Phones, etc.) need a way to add and
edit records that have more fields than a Tabulator grid row can
reasonably show inline (e.g. Tasks: description, notes, status, priority,
parent/subtask relationships).

Three approaches were considered:

1. **Inline Tabulator row editing** (`table.addRow({}, true)` + edit in
   place) — tried previously for the top-level Projects grid
   (2026-06-28) and **abandoned**: `cellEdited` does not fire reliably
   for programmatically-added rows under `dblclick` edit-trigger mode.
   Not worth retrying for Tasks; same engine, same failure mode expected.
2. **Pop open a separate full detail panel** (`openNewRecordPanel`/
   `openDetailPanel`, same as Project/Contact/Organization Add today) —
   works, but visually disconnects the task list from the task form; the
   list and the thing being edited are in different UI locations.
3. **Nested master-detail within the same tab** (chosen) — Tabulator
   list on top, a real detail form below it, both inside the same tab
   panel. Selecting or adding a row shows/edits that record in the form
   directly underneath the list it came from.

## Chosen design

Within a child datasheet tab (e.g. the Tasks tab of a Project's detail
panel):

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PROJECT detail form                       │  ← top-level panel
│  Name / Description / Type / Status        │
│  [Save] [New] [Exit]                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Tabs: Details | Tasks | Links | Contacts   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─ Tasks tab (subform of Project) ───────┐ │
│  │ Project: WCYJ Refurbs   ← context line │ │
│  │                                         │ │
│  │  Tabulator list (Tasks for Project)     │ │
│  │  [+ Add Task]                            │ │
│  │  name | status | priority | ⋯            │ │
│  ├───────────────────────────────────────────┤ │
│  │  Task detail form                        │ │
│  │  Name / Description / Status / ...       │ │
│  │  [Save] [New] [Exit]                     │ │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The Tasks tab is a **subform of the Project**, not an independent
list-plus-form floating on its own. It needs a visible reminder at the
top of the tab of which project it belongs to — separate from the
hidden `project_id` field that actually powers the save. Two purposes,
two mechanisms:

- **Hidden `project_id` field** — powers the save payload, never
  rendered as an editable control (see "Add flow" below).
- **Project-context line** ("Project: WCYJ Refurbs") — presentational
  only, reminds the person what they're looking at.

**First implementation: static text label**, rendered once when the tab
loads (project name, not a link). A future version could make this a
link/button back to the Project's own Details tab, letting someone jump
back up a level directly — deliberately deferred; try the simple label
first and see whether the need for a jump-back link actually surfaces
in practice before building it.

- **Top:** existing Tabulator child-datasheet engine (`datasheet.js` /
  `initDatasheet()`), unchanged in its own right.
- **Bottom:** **the same generic detail-panel content** already used for
  the top-level Project/Contact/Organization panel —
  `_detail_panel_content.html`, fetched via `/panel/{entity}/{id}` (or
  `/panel/{entity}/new`), rendered by `panel.py`, driven by
  `detail-panel.js`. Not a new form, not a Tasks-specific form. A second
  instance of the exact same machinery, mounted in a different DOM
  container than the top-level one.

This is a direct extension of the existing Metadata-Driven UI + ABAC
architecture: `fieldkit.py` doesn't know or care whether it's
introspecting `v_task_detail`, `v_project_detail`, or (in a future,
different deployment) `v_inventory_item_detail`. Any entity with a
proper SQL layer (`v_*_detail` view, `api.get_*_detail()`,
`api.save_*()`, `api.delete_*()`) gets this same nested master-detail
treatment for free — no new template code, no new JS, no per-entity
form.

### Why this matters beyond Tasks

This is the same principle that keeps the whole app reusable across
different database-backed deployments (the original design goal for
Curator) — and it also solves a smaller, easy-to-miss problem: keeping
different views of the same data looking consistent. Without one
canonical rendering path, it's easy for e.g. a Contacts/Organizations
bulk-datasheet view and the Identities listbox view to visually drift
from each other over time. Reusing the same detail-panel machinery
everywhere makes that consistency the default, not something that has
to be maintained by discipline.

## Per-entity judgment call

Not every child datasheet needs this. The pattern applies when a child
entity has enough fields to warrant a real form (Tasks: yes). Simpler
child entities — a couple of inline-editable columns, nothing worth
opening a separate form for (e.g. possibly Emails, Phones, URLs) — can
stay as plain Tabulator rows with no lower form at all. This is decided
per entity, not architecturally forced one way or the other.

## Behavior details (agreed)

- **Save behavior:** After saving in the lower detail form, the
  Tabulator list above **must refresh** to reflect the change — a save
  that doesn't visibly update the list above it reads as "did that
  actually save?" to the user. Use the existing
  `refresh_{containerId}()` hook already stubbed in `datasheet.js`
  (`window[`refresh_${containerId}`] = () => table.setData(ajaxUrl)`)
  to reload the list after a successful save in the nested form.
- **Selection flow:** Clicking an existing row in the Tabulator list
  fetches and displays that record in the lower form via the same
  fetch-and-swap pattern `detail-panel.js` already uses
  (`/panel/{entity}/{id}`).
- **Add flow:** `+ Add Task` opens the lower form in new-record mode
  (`/panel/{entity}/new`), with the parent FK (`project_id`) pre-filled
  as a hidden field — not user-editable, not guessed, populated from
  context. This depends on the `hidden` field type already planned for
  `fieldkit.py` (see Tasks UI wiring, item 2 in the 2026-07-08 handoff).

## Deferred

**Recursive nesting for Subtasks.** The roadmap already calls for each
Task's own detail panel to have a Subtasks child section. Whether that
means the lower task-detail form itself contains a *second* nested
instance of this same list-plus-form pattern (making it genuinely
recursive, no depth limit) is explicitly deferred. Get the one-level
parent version (Project → Tasks) fully working first; revisit Subtasks
nesting as its own follow-on design pass once that's proven out.

## Relationship to prior architecture decisions

- Builds directly on "Metadata-Driven UI with Dynamic ABAC" — the same
  vocabulary and mechanism already established for the top-level panel.
- Consistent with "one canonical path per concern," already applied
  twice this project (`_detail_panel_content.html` as the only panel
  renderer; `datasheet.js` as the only child-datasheet implementation).
- Does **not** touch `_projects_table.html` (the richer, separate
  Tabulator implementation used for the top-level Projects list). That
  unification question remains its own separate, explicitly deferred
  decision.

## 📄 pwa_deploy_notes

# Curator PWA Desktop Installer — Deployment Notes

## Current State (Dev)

A `.desktop` file launches Curator in an isolated Chrome app-mode window with no extensions, using a dedicated profile directory. Works for single-user dev on LMDE with Chrome installed at `/opt/google/chrome/google-chrome` and Curator running on `localhost:8080`.

The install script:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
cat > ~/.local/share/applications/curator.desktop << EOF
[Desktop Entry]
Version=1.0
Terminal=false
Type=Application
Name=Curator — Navigate the Project Crew
Exec=/opt/google/chrome/google-chrome --app=http://localhost:8080 --user-data-dir=/home/$USER/.config/curator-pwa-profile --disable-extensions --no-default-browser-check --no-first-run
Icon=chrome-cpdpbfelifklonephgpieimdpcecgoen-Default
StartupWMClass=crx_cpdpbfelifklonephgpieimdpcecgoen
EOF

mkdir -p /home/$USER/.config/curator-pwa-profile
chmod +x ~/.local/share/applications/curator.desktop
echo "Curator shortcut installed."
```

---

## Before Public Deployment — Things to Resolve

### 1. Chrome path varies by distro/install method
- `/opt/google/chrome/google-chrome` — Chrome via .deb on Debian/Ubuntu/LMDE
- `google-chrome` or `google-chrome-stable` — may be on PATH
- `chromium` or `chromium-browser` — Chromium (open source build)

The install script should detect which browser is available, or ask the user, rather than hardcoding the path.

### 2. Icon
The current `Icon=` value (`chrome-cpdpbfelifklonephgpieimdpcecgoen-Default`) was auto-generated when the PWA was installed in Carolyn's Default Chrome profile. It won't exist for other users.

Fix: bundle a proper Curator icon (PNG, ideally 512×512) with the installer and reference it by absolute path, e.g.:
```ini
Icon=/opt/curator/curator-icon.png
```

### 3. Port
Currently hardcoded to port 8080. If Curator moves to a different port, the installer needs to know. Consider:
- A config file or environment variable the installer reads
- Or a prompt during install

### 4. Real PWA (Option B)
For a proper installable PWA experience (OS-level app entry, offline capability, install prompt in browser), Curator needs:
- A `manifest.json` served as a static file
- A `<link rel="manifest">` in `base.html`
- Icons in multiple sizes (192×192, 512×512 minimum)
- Optionally a service worker for offline support

This is a Curator code change, scoped as its own changedoc when deployment prep begins.

### 5. Multi-browser support
The current approach is Chrome-only. For deployment to users on Firefox or other browsers, either:
- Detect the browser and generate the appropriate launch command
- Or implement Option B (real PWA manifest) which gives Firefox and other browsers a native install path

### 6. Install page — generated `.desktop` file
Add a FastAPI route (Captain-gated) that renders an install page showing the correct `.desktop` file content in a code block, pre-filled with the configured port. User copies it, pastes it into `~/.local/share/applications/curator.desktop`, and runs `chmod +x` on it. Not elegant but requires no server-side filesystem writes, no permissions complexity, and works for any user on any machine. Good fallback for tech-comfortable users until a proper installer exists.

### 7. `start.sh` integration
The desktop shortcut currently assumes Curator is already running. Eventually the `Exec=` line should call a wrapper script that:
1. Starts Curator (`start.sh` or equivalent)
2. Waits for it to be ready (poll `localhost` or use a health check endpoint)
3. Then launches the Chrome app window

```bash
#!/bin/bash
/path/to/start.sh &
# wait for Curator to be ready
until curl -s http://localhost:8080 > /dev/null; do sleep 0.5; done
exec /opt/google/chrome/google-chrome --app=http://localhost:8080 \
  --user-data-dir=/home/$USER/.config/curator-pwa-profile \
  --disable-extensions --no-default-browser-check --no-first-run
```

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_DATASHEET_JS_EXTRACTION

# Changedoc: datasheet.js Extraction + parent_field Fix

**Date:** 2026-07-08
**Depends on:** `_datasheet.html`, `_datasheet_with_header.html`, `base.html`
(all as uploaded this session)

**Scope:** Two related fixes in one unit:
1. Extract `_datasheet.html`'s inline `<script>` to a real
   `static/js/datasheet.js` ES module — same pattern as
   `bidirectional-filter.js` and `detail-panel.js`.
2. Replace the `paramKey` string-guessing heuristic with an explicit
   `parent_field` config parameter — fixes a real bug that would produce
   `task_id` instead of `project_id` for the Tasks child datasheet.

No SQL. No new routes. No `base.html` change — `datasheet.js` is imported
on demand by `_datasheet.html`'s `<script type="module">` block, not loaded
on every page the way `detail-panel.js` is (same lazy-import pattern
`_tab_identities.html` already uses for `bidirectional-filter.js`).

**Known gaps NOT fixed in this changedoc (logged separately):**
- `_datasheet.html`'s save/delete calls hit `/api/{entity}/save` and
  `/api/{entity}/{id}` — routes that don't exist; real routes are under
  `/crew/{entity}/...`. Fix deferred to next session.
- `_datasheet_with_header.html`'s `+ Add` button does nothing — its
  `<script type="module">` block is explicitly empty. Fix deferred to
  next session.

---

## The `paramKey` bug, precisely

```js
// BEFORE — in _datasheet.html's inline <script>
const paramKey = '{{ entity }}'.replace(/s$/, '_id')
    .replace('contact_email', 'contact')
    .replace('contact_phone', 'contact');
```

For `entity='tasks'`, this produces `task_id` — but the actual foreign key
column for a task's parent project is `project_id`. The result: every new
task row created through a child datasheet would send `{"task_id": 12}`
instead of `{"project_id": 12}`, silently saving the wrong field (or, more
likely, the proc ignoring it and creating an orphaned record).

The fix: `parent_field` is passed explicitly by whoever includes the
datasheet, the same way `entity`/`query_name`/`columns` already are. No
guessing from string patterns, no hardcoded special cases.

---

## Apply order

Three file changes, no pgAdmin steps:
1. Create `static/js/datasheet.js` (new file)
2. Replace `_datasheet.html`
3. Replace `_datasheet_with_header.html`

Then restart uvicorn and verify (see bottom of doc).

---

## `static/js/datasheet.js` (new file)

```javascript
/**
 * datasheet.js
 *
 * Generic Tabulator child-datasheet engine for Curator.
 * Called by _datasheet.html's <script type="module"> block on every
 * panel tab that includes a child datasheet (Tasks, Emails, Phones,
 * URLs, Contacts, etc.).
 *
 * Usage (from _datasheet.html's generated module script):
 *
 *   import { initDatasheet } from '/static/js/datasheet.js';
 *
 *   initDatasheet({
 *     containerId:  'tasks-datasheet',
 *     entity:       'tasks',
 *     queryName:    'for_project',
 *     queryParams:  '12',
 *     columns:      [...],
 *     parentField:  'project_id',   // explicit FK — never guessed
 *   });
 *
 * Known gaps (see CHANGEDOC_DATASHEET_JS_EXTRACTION.md):
 *   - save/delete URLs are /api/{entity}/... — routes that don't exist yet.
 *     Real routes live under /crew/{entity}/... Fix in next changedoc.
 *   - + Add button wiring is deferred — same next changedoc.
 */

export function initDatasheet(config) {
    const {
        containerId,
        entity,
        queryName,
        queryParams,
        columns,
        parentField,  // explicit parent FK field name — required for INSERT
                      // to include the correct parent id in the payload.
                      // Pass '' or omit if this datasheet has no parent FK.
    } = config;

    const container = document.getElementById(containerId);
    if (!container) return;

    const ajaxUrl = `/api/query/${entity}/${queryName}?params=${queryParams}`;

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Save a row to the server
    // NOTE: URLs below (/api/{entity}/...) do not exist in the current app —
    // real routes are /crew/{entity}/... This is a known gap, not addressed
    // in this changedoc. Saving will 404 until the URL fix lands.
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    async function saveRow(row) {
        const data = row.getData();
        const isNew = !data.id;

        // Don't save a new row with no content — just delete it
        const firstEditable = columns.find(c => c.editor);
        if (isNew && firstEditable && !data[firstEditable.field]) {
            row.delete();
            return true;
        }

        const url = isNew
            ? `/api/${entity}/save`
            : `/api/${entity}/${data.id}/save`;

        // Only send editable columns
        const editableFields = columns
            .filter(c => c.editor && c.field !== 'id')
            .map(c => c.field);

        const payload = {};
        editableFields.forEach(f => { payload[f] = data[f] ?? null; });

        // For new rows, include the parent FK with its explicit field name.
        // parentField replaces the old string-guessing heuristic that produced
        // task_id instead of project_id for the Tasks entity.
        if (isNew && parentField && queryParams) {
            payload[parentField] = queryParams;
        }

        const resp = await fetch(url, {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
            body: JSON.stringify(payload),
        });

        if (!resp.ok) {
            const err = await resp.json().catch(() => ({ detail: resp.statusText }));
            alert(err.detail || 'Save failed');
            return false;
        }

        const saved = await resp.json();
        row.update(saved);
        return true;
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Delete a row from the server
    // NOTE: Same URL gap as saveRow above.
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    async function deleteRow(row) {
        const id = row.getData().id;
        if (!id) { row.delete(); return; }

        if (!confirm('Delete this row?')) return;

        const resp = await fetch(`/api/${entity}/${id}`, { method: 'DELETE' });
        if (resp.ok) {
            row.delete();
        } else {
            alert('Delete failed');
        }
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Tabulator init — uses global Tabulator loaded by base.html via CDN
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    const table = new Tabulator(container, {  // eslint-disable-line no-undef
        height: '100%',
        layout: 'fitColumns',
        ajaxURL: ajaxUrl,
        ajaxConfig: { headers: { 'Accept': 'application/json' } },
        ajaxResponse: (url, params, response) => response.records || [],
        editTriggerEvent: 'dblclick',
        columns: columns,

        cellEdited: async function(cell) {
            await saveRow(cell.getRow());
        },

        rowContextMenu: [
            {
                label: 'Delete row',
                action: (e, row) => deleteRow(row),
            }
        ],

        dataLoadError: (error) => {
            console.error(`Failed to load ${entity}/${queryName}:`, error);
        },
    });

    // Escape — delete empty new row, or cancel edit
    document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
        if (e.key === 'Escape') {
            const newRow = table.getRows().find(r => !r.getData().id);
            if (newRow) newRow.delete();
        }
    });

    // Store reference on window for parent access (e.g. refresh after save)
    window[`tabulator_${containerId}`] = table;
    window[`refresh_${containerId}`]   = () => table.setData(ajaxUrl);
}
```

## `_datasheet.html`

### BEFORE

```jinja
{#
  _datasheet.html
  
  Reusable Tabulator datasheet grid.
  
  This partial renders just the Tabulator instance. It is always used as
  a child of _datasheet_with_header.html (which provides the + button,
  search, and controls).
  
  Parameters:
    - container_id (str): DOM id for Tabulator to mount to (required)
    - entity (str): QueryLoader entity name (e.g., "tasks", "contact_emails")
    - query_name (str): QueryLoader query name (e.g., "for_project")
    - query_params (str): Comma-separated bind parameters (e.g., "123")
    - columns (list): Column definitions for Tabulator
    - save_url (str): POST endpoint for saving row edits
    - add_url (str, optional): POST endpoint for adding new rows
  
  Example usage (from _datasheet_with_header.html):
    
    {% include '_datasheet.html' with
        container_id='tasks-datasheet',
        entity='tasks',
        query_name='for_project',
        query_params=record.id,
        columns=[
          { "title": "Name", "field": "name", "width": 200, "editor": "input" },
          { "title": "Status", "field": "status_id", "width": 100 }
        ],
        save_url='/crew/tasks/save'
    %}
#}

<div id="{{ container_id }}" style="height: 100%;"></div>

<script>
window.addEventListener('load', function () {

  const container = document.getElementById('{{ container_id }}');
  const entity = '{{ entity }}';
  const queryName = '{{ query_name }}';
  const queryParams = '{{ query_params }}';
  const ajaxUrl = `/api/query/${entity}/${queryName}?params=${queryParams}`;

  const columns = {{ columns | tojson }};

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Save a row to the server via generic entity endpoint
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  async function saveRow(row) {
    const data = row.getData();
    const isNew = !data.id;

    // Don't save a new row with no content — just delete it
    const firstEditable = columns.find(c => c.editor);
    if (isNew && firstEditable && !data[firstEditable.field]) {
      row.delete();
      return true;
    }

    const url = isNew
      ? `/api/${entity}/save`
      : `/api/${entity}/${data.id}/save`;

    // Only send editable columns
    const editableFields = columns
      .filter(c => c.editor && c.field !== 'id')
      .map(c => c.field);

    const payload = {};
    editableFields.forEach(f => { payload[f] = data[f] ?? null; });

    // For new rows, also include the parent foreign key if present
    // (e.g. contact_id, project_id — passed in via query_params)
    {% if query_params %}
    if (isNew) {
      const paramKey = '{{ entity }}'.replace(/s$/, '_id').replace('contact_email', 'contact').replace('contact_phone', 'contact');
      if (paramKey && !payload[paramKey]) {
        payload[paramKey] = {{ query_params }};
      }
    }
    {% endif %}

    const resp = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
    });

    if (!resp.ok) {
      const err = await resp.json().catch(() => ({ detail: resp.statusText }));
      alert(err.detail || 'Save failed');
      return false;
    }

    const saved = await resp.json();
    row.update(saved);
    return true;
  }

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Delete a row from the server
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  async function deleteRow(row) {
    const id = row.getData().id;
    if (!id) { row.delete(); return; }

    if (!confirm('Delete this row?')) return;

    const resp = await fetch(`/api/${entity}/${id}`, { method: 'DELETE' });
    if (resp.ok) {
      row.delete();
    } else {
      alert('Delete failed');
    }
  }

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Tabulator init — uses global Tabulator loaded by base.html via CDN
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  const table = new Tabulator(container, {
    height: '100%',
    layout: 'fitColumns',
    ajaxURL: ajaxUrl,
    ajaxConfig: { headers: { 'Accept': 'application/json' } },
    ajaxResponse: (url, params, response) => response.records || [],
    editTriggerEvent: 'dblclick',
    columns: columns,

    // Auto-save when a cell edit is confirmed (Enter or click away)
    cellEdited: async function(cell) {
      await saveRow(cell.getRow());
    },

    rowContextMenu: [
      {
        label: 'Delete row',
        action: (e, row) => deleteRow(row),
      }
    ],

    dataLoadError: (error) => {
      console.error(`Failed to load ${entity}/${queryName}:`, error);
    },
  });

  // Esc — delete empty new row, or cancel
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      // Find any unsaved new row and remove it
      const newRow = table.getRows().find(r => !r.getData().id);
      if (newRow) {
        newRow.delete();
      }
    }
  });

  // Store reference on window for parent access (e.g. refresh after external save)
  window[`tabulator_${container.id}`] = table;
  window[`refresh_${container.id}`] = () => table.setData(ajaxUrl);

});
</script>
```

### AFTER

```jinja
{#
  _datasheet.html

  Reusable Tabulator child-datasheet grid.

  Always used as a child of _datasheet_with_header.html (which provides
  the + Add button, search, and controls). Renders a mount point div and
  a small module script that imports initDatasheet() from datasheet.js —
  same pattern as _tab_identities.html → bidirectional-filter.js.

  The full Tabulator init, save, delete, and Escape-key logic lives in
  datasheet.js, not here. This file's only job is passing Jinja-rendered
  config values (which only exist at template-render time) into a call
  to that module.

  Parameters:
    - container_id  (str)  — DOM id for Tabulator to mount to (required)
    - entity        (str)  — QueryLoader entity name (e.g. "tasks")
    - query_name    (str)  — QueryLoader query name (e.g. "for_project")
    - query_params  (str)  — Comma-separated bind parameters (e.g. "123")
    - columns       (list) — Tabulator column definitions
    - parent_field  (str)  — Explicit FK column name for new-row inserts
                             (e.g. "project_id" for tasks, "contact_id"
                             for contact_emails). Never guessed from entity
                             name. Pass '' if this datasheet has no parent.
#}

<div id="{{ container_id }}" style="height: 100%;"></div>

<script type="module">
import { initDatasheet } from '/static/js/datasheet.js';

initDatasheet({
    containerId:  '{{ container_id }}',
    entity:       '{{ entity }}',
    queryName:    '{{ query_name }}',
    queryParams:  '{{ query_params }}',
    columns:      {{ columns | tojson }},
    parentField:  '{{ parent_field | default("") }}',
});
</script>
```

**Why:** The entire `<script>` block (save/delete logic, Tabulator init,
Escape handler, window references — ~80 lines) is now in one shared
`datasheet.js` that every child datasheet imports, instead of being
re-emitted verbatim into the page's HTML once per included datasheet.
`save_url`/`add_url` are removed — `save_url` was documented but never
actually used in the script (the URL was always hardcoded from `entity`),
and `add_url` belongs to `_datasheet_with_header.html`'s + Add button,
not the grid itself.

**Why:** `save_url` removed from the `{% with %}` passthrough — it was

that don't supply it don't error. The empty `<script type="module">` block

script tag is worse than nothing, since it implies something is wired when
it isn't.

## `base.html`

No change. `datasheet.js` is an ES module imported on demand by
`_datasheet.html`'s `<script type="module">` — the browser fetches it
only when a panel tab containing a child datasheet is actually rendered.
It doesn't need a `<script src>` tag in `base.html` the way
`detail-panel.js` does (which is loaded on every page because any page
may open a detail panel).

---

## Verify after applying

1. Restart uvicorn, hard-refresh the browser.
2. Open a project's detail panel — the Tasks tab should show "Tasks —
   coming soon" placeholder (no JS errors in the console from the new
   import, since the tab panel exists in the DOM even if empty).
3. Open DevTools → Network → filter by `datasheet.js` — confirm it's
   NOT fetched on initial page load (lazy import, only fetched when a
   tab including `_datasheet.html` is actually rendered).
4. `pylint src/` — no Python changes, should still be 10.00/10.
5. `pytest` — no changes affecting test coverage.

**Note:** Because the save/delete URL bug is deferred, you cannot yet
verify that row edits actually save — they'll 404. That's expected and
documented. The extraction itself (module loads, Tabulator inits, no
console errors) is what this changedoc verifies.

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_DETAIL_PANEL_CONTENT_SPLIT

# Changedoc: Detail Panel Content Split (Bug Fix) — REVISED

**Date:** 2026-07-06 (continued session)
**Supersedes:** the earlier same-titled changedoc from this session — do
not apply that one, apply this one instead. Same bug, cleaner fix.
**Depends on:** `_detail_panel.html`, `panel.py`, `_form_actions.html`,
`crew.html` (all as uploaded this session)

**Scope:** Bug fix + a small cleanup the bug fix surfaced. No SQL, no new
routes.

---

## The bug, precisely

`crew.html` includes `_detail_panel.html` once at initial page load,
hardcoded to `entity='projects'`. But that render is **never visible** —
the panel sits hidden behind the hero image until someone clicks `⋯` or
`+ Add`, at which point `detail-panel.js`'s `fetchAndSwapPanel()` replaces
`.detail-panel`'s entire `innerHTML` with whatever `panel.py` returns from
`/panel/{entity}/{id}` (or `.../new`).

`panel.py` was only ever rendering `_detail_form_fields.html` — bare field
`<div>`s, no tab bar, no `<form>` wrapper, no close button — because
`_detail_panel_content.html`, the file it was seemingly written assuming
existed, was never actually created. So the correct tab bar from the
invisible initial render gets wiped out the moment anyone opens anything,
replaced by three bare `.form-group` divs. Confirmed via DOM inspection
after a full uvicorn restart and browser cache clear — not staleness, a
genuine mismatch between what `detail-panel.js` assumes `panel.py` returns
and what it actually returns.

## The cleanup this surfaced

Once `_detail_panel_content.html` exists and `panel.py` is the *only* thing
that renders real content into `.detail-panel`, `crew.html`'s initial-load
render of `_detail_panel.html` has no job left to do — it's invisible,
gets fully overwritten on first open regardless, and was hardcoding a fake
`entity='projects'` plus forwarding `project_types`/`project_statuses` that
`_detail_panel_content.html` doesn't even reference (fieldkit replaced that
raw-lookup approach already). Keeping it "just in case" would mean two
different code paths capable of rendering this panel's content — exactly
the duplication fieldkit's whole design was meant to eliminate, even if
one path is currently invisible. So it's removed outright, not defended
against with default-value fallbacks.

---

## The fix

1. **New `_detail_panel_content.html`** — the tab bar + form + child-tab
   placeholders + action buttons, extracted from `_detail_panel.html`.
   This is what `panel.py` renders on every real panel open.
2. **`_detail_panel.html` becomes a genuinely empty shell** — no
   entity/record data at all. Just the outer div, rendered once,
   invisible, immediately superseded on first open.
3. **`crew.html`'s include simplifies** — drops the `{% with entity=...,
   record_id=..., record={}, project_types=..., project_statuses=... %}`
   wrapper entirely; just includes the now-parameterless shell.
4. **`panel.py` renders `_detail_panel_content.html` instead of
   `_detail_form_fields.html`**, loading `actions`/`container_class` via
   `FormActions.from_yaml()` the same way `crew.py` already does — confirmed
   against the real `formkit.py` (`from_yaml()` returns exactly
   `{"container_class": ..., "actions": [...]}`, matching what
   `_form_actions.html` expects).

`_detail_panel_content.html` still defaults `fields`/`options`/`record`/
`actions` to empty values — not to support two callers gracefully anymore
(there's only one real caller, `panel.py`, which always supplies full
data), but because the shell's one harmless initial-load render passes
nothing at all, and Jinja raises on iterating an undefined variable
(`{% for field in fields %}`) even though it happily prints one as empty
text. The defaults are a two-line safety net for that one invisible
render, not a design accommodation.

---

## Apply order

No SQL, no pgAdmin steps. Four file changes below, then restart uvicorn
and hard-refresh the browser.

---

## `_detail_panel_content.html` (new file)

```jinja
{#
  _detail_panel_content.html

  The actual rendered content of a detail panel for one entity + record:
  tab navigation, the Details tab (fieldkit-driven form), the
  currently-placeholder child tabs, and the action button bar.

  panel.py is the ONLY renderer of this template with real data — every
  /panel/{entity}/{id} (or .../new) request re-renders this exact
  content, and detail-panel.js's fetchAndSwapPanel() replaces
  .detail-panel's entire innerHTML with the result. _detail_panel.html's
  own initial-page-load render includes this template with nothing —
  invisible, immediately overwritten on first open — which is why the
  defaults below exist.

  Parameters (all optional — panel.py always supplies them; only
  _detail_panel.html's invisible initial render omits them):
    - entity          (str)  — "projects", "contacts", or "organizations"
    - record_id       (int|str) — blank/'' for a new-record panel
    - record          (dict, optional) — current field values, defaults {}
    - fields          (list[FieldDef], optional) — from FieldKit.fields,
                      defaults []
    - options         (dict, optional) — FieldKit.options, source name ->
                      list of {"value","label"} dicts, defaults {}
    - actions         (list, optional) — from formkit.FormActions, for
                      _form_actions.html, defaults []
    - container_class (str, optional) — for _form_actions.html
#}
{% set fields = fields|default([]) %}
{% set options = options|default({}) %}
{% set record = record|default({}) %}
{% set actions = actions|default([]) %}

<!-- Tab navigation -->
<div class="detail-tabs">
  <button class="detail-tab-button active" data-tab="details">Details</button>

  {% if entity == "projects" %}
    <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="tasks">Tasks</button>
    <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="links">Links</button>
    <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="contacts">Contacts</button>
  {% elif entity == "contacts" %}
    <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="emails">Emails</button>
    <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="phones">Phones</button>
    <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="urls">URLs</button>
    <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="organizations">Organizations</button>
  {% elif entity == "organizations" %}
    <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="contacts">Contacts</button>
  {% endif %}

  <button class="detail-close-button" aria-label="Close detail panel">×</button>
</div>

<!-- Tab content container -->
<div class="detail-tab-panels">

  <!-- ===== DETAILS TAB (always first) ===== -->
  <div class="detail-tab-panel active" data-tab="details">
    <form id="detail-form" class="detail-form" data-entity="{{ entity }}" data-id="{{ record_id }}">
      <div id="detail-form-fields">
        {% include "partials/_detail_form_fields.html" %}
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>

  <!-- ===== CHILD TABS (deferred) ===== -->
  {% if entity == "projects" %}
    <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="tasks">
      <p class="tab-placeholder">Tasks — coming soon</p>
    </div>
    <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="links">
      <p class="tab-placeholder">Links — coming soon</p>
    </div>
    <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="contacts">
      <p class="tab-placeholder">Contacts — coming soon</p>
    </div>

  {% elif entity == "contacts" %}
    <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="emails">
      <p class="tab-placeholder">Emails — coming soon</p>
    </div>
    <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="phones">
      <p class="tab-placeholder">Phones — coming soon</p>
    </div>
    <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="urls">
      <p class="tab-placeholder">URLs — coming soon</p>
    </div>
    <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="organizations">
      <p class="tab-placeholder">Organizations — coming soon</p>
    </div>

  {% elif entity == "organizations" %}
    <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="contacts">
      <p class="tab-placeholder">Contacts — coming soon</p>
    </div>
  {% endif %}

</div>

<!-- Action buttons: sticky footer -->
{% include 'partials/_form_actions.html' %}
```

## `_detail_panel.html`

### BEFORE

```jinja
{#
  _detail_panel.html

  Detail panel — displays a record's details in a tabbed interface.
  Replaces the hero image when a user clicks ⋯ on a datasheet row.

  Parameters:
    - entity    (str) — "projects", "contacts", or "organizations"
    - record_id (int) — ID of the record being displayed (blank/'' for
                        a new-record panel not yet opened)

  The details tab's field inputs are NOT rendered here anymore — see
  detail-form-fields below. detail-panel.js fetches them from
  /panel/{entity}/{id} (or /panel/{entity}/new) on every panel open,
  fetch-and-swap style, so this template only needs entity/record_id to
  set data attributes for JS to read. The panel is hidden behind the
  hero image until an open action fires, so there's nothing visible to
  lose by leaving detail-form-fields empty at initial page render.

  Child datasheets (Tasks, Emails, etc.) are deferred — coming soon —
  and unrelated to this fetch-and-swap change.
#}

<div class="detail-panel" data-entity="{{ entity }}" data-id="{{ record_id }}">

  <!-- Tab navigation -->
  <div class="detail-tabs">
    <button class="detail-tab-button active" data-tab="details">Details</button>

    {% if entity == "projects" %}
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="tasks">Tasks</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="links">Links</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="contacts">Contacts</button>
    {% elif entity == "contacts" %}
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="emails">Emails</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="phones">Phones</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="urls">URLs</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="organizations">Organizations</button>
    {% elif entity == "organizations" %}
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="contacts">Contacts</button>
    {% endif %}

    <button class="detail-close-button" aria-label="Close detail panel">×</button>
  </div>

  <!-- Tab content container -->
  <div class="detail-tab-panels">

    <!-- ===== DETAILS TAB (always first) ===== -->
    <div class="detail-tab-panel active" data-tab="details">
      <form id="detail-form" class="detail-form" data-entity="{{ entity }}" data-id="{{ record_id }}">
        <div id="detail-form-fields">
          <!-- Populated by detail-panel.js fetching
               /panel/{entity}/{id} or /panel/{entity}/new on open. -->
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>

    <!-- ===== CHILD TABS (deferred) ===== -->
    {% if entity == "projects" %}
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="tasks">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Tasks — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="links">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Links — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="contacts">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Contacts — coming soon</p>
      </div>

    {% elif entity == "contacts" %}
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="emails">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Emails — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="phones">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Phones — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="urls">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">URLs — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="organizations">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Organizations — coming soon</p>
      </div>

    {% elif entity == "organizations" %}
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="contacts">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Contacts — coming soon</p>
      </div>
    {% endif %}

  </div>

  <!-- Action buttons: sticky footer — actions and container_class from route -->
  {% include 'partials/_form_actions.html' %}

</div>
```

### AFTER

```jinja
{#
  _detail_panel.html

  Genuinely empty shell for the detail panel container — no entity,
  no record data. This is the ONE render of this file that happens via
  crew.html at initial page load, and it's invisible: the panel sits
  hidden behind the hero image until someone clicks ⋯ or + Add. From
  that point on, panel.py is the sole renderer of real content —
  /panel/{entity}/{id} (or .../new) returns _detail_panel_content.html
  fully populated, and detail-panel.js's fetchAndSwapPanel() replaces
  this div's entire innerHTML with it.

  Previously received entity='projects'/record_id=0/record={}/
  project_types/project_statuses from crew.html — all vestigial.
  project_types/project_statuses aren't referenced anywhere in
  _detail_panel_content.html (fieldkit replaced that raw-lookup
  approach), and entity/record_id were rendering a fake "projects"
  panel nobody ever saw before panel.py overwrote it on first open.
  Removed outright rather than defended against with fallback values —
  a second code path capable of rendering this content, even one that's
  invisible, is exactly the duplication fieldkit's design was meant to
  eliminate.
#}

<div class="detail-panel" data-entity="" data-id="">
  {% include "partials/_detail_panel_content.html" %}
</div>
```

## `crew.html`

### BEFORE

```jinja
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block title %}{{ role_title }} — Curator{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<section class="crew-section {{ role }}">

    <!-- Hero image and detail panel share the same spot; toggle visibility -->
    <div class="hero-detail-stack">
        {% with
            role=role,
            hero_image=role + ".png",
            title=role_title,
            show_back=true
        %}
            {% include "partials/_crew_header.html" %}
        {% endwith %}

        <div id="detail-panel-container">
            {% with entity='projects', record_id=0, record={}, project_types=project_types, project_statuses=project_statuses %}
                {% include "partials/_detail_panel.html" %}
            {% endwith %}
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Tab Navigation -->
    <div class="tabs">
        {% for tab in tabs %}
            <button
                class="tab-btn {% if loop.first %}active{% endif %}"
                data-tab="tab-{{ tab.id }}"
            >{{ tab.label }}</button>
        {% endfor %}
    </div>

    <!-- Tab Panels -->
    {% for tab in tabs %}
        <div id="tab-{{ tab.id }}" class="tab-panel {% if loop.first %}active{% endif %}">
            {% include "partials/" + tab.template %}
        </div>
    {% endfor %}

</section>

<!-- Embed lookups for Tabulator and identity panels -->
<script>
    window.projectTypes    = {{ project_types    | tojson }};
    window.projectStatuses = {{ project_statuses | tojson }};

    // Tab switching
    document.querySelectorAll('.tab-btn').forEach(btn => {
        btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            document.querySelectorAll('.tab-panel').forEach(p => p.classList.remove('active'));
            document.querySelectorAll('.tab-btn').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
            document.getElementById(this.dataset.tab).classList.add('active');
            this.classList.add('active');
        });
    });
</script>
{% endblock %}
```

## `panel.py`

### BEFORE

```python
"""Detail panel field-fragment routes.

Serves a single entity's field-input fragment, rendered via fieldkit,
for detail-panel.js to fetch-and-swap into the form container on every
panel open (new record or existing). Replaces the old approach of one
static per-entity form baked into _detail_panel.html at page load.

Mirrors crew.py's raw jinja2.Environment setup rather than introducing
FastAPI's Jinja2Templates as a second templating convention.
"""

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db
from curator.web.routes.contacts import _fetch_contact_for_display
from curator.web.routes.organizations import _fetch_organization_for_display
from curator.web.routes.projects import _fetch_project_for_display

TEMPLATES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "templates"
env = Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(TEMPLATES_DIR))

router = APIRouter()

# Entity name -> its _fetch_*_for_display function. Small, fixed set of
# wiring decisions, same reasoning as app.py's _FIELDKIT_VIEWS: adding
# an entity means adding routes/templates alongside it regardless, so
# there's no scenario where this changes without a code change too.
_FETCH_FUNCTIONS = {
    "projects": _fetch_project_for_display,
    "contacts": _fetch_contact_for_display,
    "organizations": _fetch_organization_for_display,
}


def _render_fields(request: Request, entity: str, record: dict) -> HTMLResponse:
    """Render the field-fragment template for one entity + record.

    Args:
        request: Current request — used to reach app.state.fieldkit,
                 the FieldKit cache built once at FastAPI startup.
        entity:  One of "projects", "contacts", "organizations".
        record:  Field values dict, or {} for a new record.

    Returns:
        HTMLResponse — the rendered fragment, ready to be swapped into
        #detail-form-fields by detail-panel.js.
    """
    kit = request.app.state.fieldkit[entity]
    template = env.get_template("partials/_detail_form_fields.html")
    return HTMLResponse(
        template.render(fields=kit.fields, record=record, options=kit.options)
    )


# /panel/{entity}/new must be declared before /panel/{entity}/{record_id}
# — same route-ordering rule as the save routes (literal before
# parameterized), otherwise FastAPI tries to parse "new" as an int and
# 422s instead of matching this route.

@router.get("/panel/{entity}/new")
async def panel_new(entity: str, request: Request):
    """Render the field fragment for a new, empty record."""
    if entity not in _FETCH_FUNCTIONS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown entity: {entity}")
    return _render_fields(request, entity, {})


@router.get("/panel/{entity}/{record_id}")
async def panel_existing(
    entity: str,
    record_id: int,
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Render the field fragment for an existing record."""
    if entity not in _FETCH_FUNCTIONS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown entity: {entity}")

    fetch_fn = _FETCH_FUNCTIONS[entity]
    record = await fetch_fn(db, record_id)
    if not record:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"{entity.title()} not found")

    return _render_fields(request, entity, record)
```

### AFTER

```python
"""Detail panel content routes.

Serves a single entity's full panel content (tab bar, fieldkit-driven
form, child-tab placeholders, action buttons), rendered via
_detail_panel_content.html, for detail-panel.js to fetch-and-swap into
.detail-panel on every panel open (new record or existing).

Previously rendered only _detail_form_fields.html — the bare field
<div>s, no tab bar or form wrapper — which silently wiped out the tab
bar on every open, since detail-panel.js replaces .detail-panel's
entire innerHTML. Fixed by rendering the same content template
_detail_panel.html's (now-empty, invisible) initial render delegates
to. See CHANGEDOC_DETAIL_PANEL_CONTENT_SPLIT.md for the full diagnosis.

Mirrors crew.py's raw jinja2.Environment setup rather than introducing
FastAPI's Jinja2Templates as a second templating convention.
"""

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.formkit import FormActions
from curator.web.deps import get_db
from curator.web.routes.contacts import _fetch_contact_for_display
from curator.web.routes.organizations import _fetch_organization_for_display
from curator.web.routes.projects import _fetch_project_for_display

TEMPLATES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "templates"
_FORMS_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "data" / "forms.yaml"
env = Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(TEMPLATES_DIR))

router = APIRouter()

# Entity name -> its _fetch_*_for_display function. Small, fixed set of
# wiring decisions, same reasoning as app.py's _FIELDKIT_VIEWS: adding
# an entity means adding routes/templates alongside it regardless, so
# there's no scenario where this changes without a code change too.
_FETCH_FUNCTIONS = {
    "projects": _fetch_project_for_display,
    "contacts": _fetch_contact_for_display,
    "organizations": _fetch_organization_for_display,
}


def _render_panel_content(
    request: Request, entity: str, record: dict, record_id
) -> HTMLResponse:
    """Render the full panel-content template for one entity + record.

    Args:
        request:   Current request — used to reach app.state.fieldkit,
                   the FieldKit cache built once at FastAPI startup.
        entity:    One of "projects", "contacts", "organizations".
        record:    Field values dict, or {} for a new record.
        record_id: The record's id, or '' for a new record — set on
                   the <form> data attributes JS reads.

    Returns:
        HTMLResponse — the rendered content (tab bar, form, child-tab
        placeholders, action buttons), ready to be swapped into
        .detail-panel's innerHTML by detail-panel.js.
    """
    kit = request.app.state.fieldkit[entity]
    detail_panel_actions = FormActions.from_yaml(_FORMS_PATH, "detail_panel")
    template = env.get_template("partials/_detail_panel_content.html")
    return HTMLResponse(
        template.render(
            entity=entity,
            record_id=record_id,
            record=record,
            fields=kit.fields,
            options=kit.options,
            actions=detail_panel_actions["actions"],
            container_class=detail_panel_actions["container_class"],
        )
    )


# /panel/{entity}/new must be declared before /panel/{entity}/{record_id}
# — same route-ordering rule as the save routes (literal before
# parameterized), otherwise FastAPI tries to parse "new" as an int and
# 422s instead of matching this route.

@router.get("/panel/{entity}/new")
async def panel_new(entity: str, request: Request):
    """Render the full panel content for a new, empty record."""
    if entity not in _FETCH_FUNCTIONS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown entity: {entity}")
    return _render_panel_content(request, entity, {}, "")


@router.get("/panel/{entity}/{record_id}")
async def panel_existing(
    entity: str,
    record_id: int,
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Render the full panel content for an existing record."""
    if entity not in _FETCH_FUNCTIONS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown entity: {entity}")

    fetch_fn = _FETCH_FUNCTIONS[entity]
    record = await fetch_fn(db, record_id)
    if not record:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"{entity.title()} not found")

    return _render_panel_content(request, entity, record, record_id)
```

**Why:** `_render_fields` is renamed `_render_panel_content` since it now
renders considerably more than fields. Confirmed against the real
`formkit.py` this time — `from_yaml()` returns
`{"container_class": str, "actions": [dict, ...]}`, each action dict having
`label`/`type`/`class`/`id`/`title`/`form_id`/`data_attrs`, an exact match
for `_form_actions.html`'s expectations.

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_DETAIL_PANEL_CONTENT_SPLIT

# Changedoc: Detail Panel Content Split (Bug Fix)

**Date:** 2026-07-06 (continued session)
**Depends on:** `_detail_panel.html`, `panel.py`, `_form_actions.html`,
`crew.html` (all as uploaded this session)

**Scope:** Fixes a real bug found while starting the Tasks work — not a
Tasks feature change. No SQL, no new routes.

---

## The bug, precisely

`crew.html` includes `_detail_panel.html` once at initial page load — full
tab bar, form wrapper, close button, everything. That render is correct.

But `detail-panel.js`'s `fetchAndSwapPanel()` replaces `.detail-panel`'s
entire `innerHTML` on every subsequent open (`⋯` on a row, or `+ Add`), using
whatever `panel.py` returns from `/panel/{entity}/{id}` (or `.../new`).
`panel.py` was only ever rendering `_detail_form_fields.html` — the bare
field `<div>`s — not the tab bar, not the `<form>` wrapper, not the close
button. So the first time anyone opens *any* record, the correct tab bar
from initial page load gets wiped out and replaced with three bare
`.form-group` divs and nothing else. Confirmed against two screenshots and
a DOM inspection after a full uvicorn restart and browser cache clear — not
a stale-file or caching issue, a genuine mismatch between what
`detail-panel.js` assumes `panel.py` returns and what it actually returns.

`_detail_panel_content.html` — the file `panel.py` was seemingly written
assuming already existed — was never actually created.

---

## The fix

1. **New `_detail_panel_content.html`** — the actual tab bar + form +
   child-tab-placeholder + action-button markup, extracted from
   `_detail_panel.html`. This is what gets re-rendered on every panel open.
2. **`_detail_panel.html` shrinks to a bare shell** — just the outer
   `<div class="detail-panel">` wrapping one include of
   `_detail_panel_content.html`. Used only by `crew.html`'s initial
   page-load render.
3. **`panel.py` renders `_detail_panel_content.html` instead of
   `_detail_form_fields.html`**, and now loads `actions`/`container_class`
   via `FormActions.from_yaml()` the same way `crew.py` already does, so the
   Save/New/Exit buttons survive the swap too.

One consequence worth calling out: since `panel.py` now renders the whole
content template — fields already included — the old `#detail-form-fields`
placeholder div (previously left empty for a second JS-driven fetch that
never actually happened) is now filled directly via
`{% include "partials/_detail_form_fields.html" %}` in the same render pass.
One fetch, fully rendered — matching what `detail-panel.js`'s own comments
already assumed was happening.

`crew.html`'s initial-page-load include only passes `entity`/`record_id`/
`record`/`project_types`/`project_statuses` — no `fields`/`options`/
`actions`. That's fine (the panel is hidden behind the hero image at that
point and gets fully replaced the first time it's opened), but
`_detail_panel_content.html` defaults all of those to safe empty values so
that initial render doesn't error.

---

## Apply order

No SQL, no pgAdmin steps. Just the three file changes below, then restart
uvicorn and hard-refresh the browser.

---
