## `_detail_panel.html`

### BEFORE

```jinja
{#
  _detail_panel.html

  Detail panel — displays a record's details in a tabbed interface.
  Replaces the hero image when a user clicks ⋯ on a datasheet row.

  Parameters:
    - entity    (str) — "projects", "contacts", or "organizations"
    - record_id (int) — ID of the record being displayed (blank/'' for
                        a new-record panel not yet opened)

  The details tab's field inputs are NOT rendered here anymore — see
  detail-form-fields below. detail-panel.js fetches them from
  /panel/{entity}/{id} (or /panel/{entity}/new) on every panel open,
  fetch-and-swap style, so this template only needs entity/record_id to
  set data attributes for JS to read. The panel is hidden behind the
  hero image until an open action fires, so there's nothing visible to
  lose by leaving detail-form-fields empty at initial page render.

  Child datasheets (Tasks, Emails, etc.) are deferred — coming soon —
  and unrelated to this fetch-and-swap change.
#}

<div class="detail-panel" data-entity="{{ entity }}" data-id="{{ record_id }}">

  <!-- Tab navigation -->
  <div class="detail-tabs">
    <button class="detail-tab-button active" data-tab="details">Details</button>

    {% if entity == "projects" %}
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="tasks">Tasks</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="links">Links</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="contacts">Contacts</button>
    {% elif entity == "contacts" %}
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="emails">Emails</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="phones">Phones</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="urls">URLs</button>
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="organizations">Organizations</button>
    {% elif entity == "organizations" %}
      <button class="detail-tab-button" data-tab="contacts">Contacts</button>
    {% endif %}

    <button class="detail-close-button" aria-label="Close detail panel">×</button>
  </div>

  <!-- Tab content container -->
  <div class="detail-tab-panels">

    <!-- ===== DETAILS TAB (always first) ===== -->
    <div class="detail-tab-panel active" data-tab="details">
      <form id="detail-form" class="detail-form" data-entity="{{ entity }}" data-id="{{ record_id }}">
        <div id="detail-form-fields">
          <!-- Populated by detail-panel.js fetching
               /panel/{entity}/{id} or /panel/{entity}/new on open. -->
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>

    <!-- ===== CHILD TABS (deferred) ===== -->
    {% if entity == "projects" %}
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="tasks">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Tasks — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="links">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Links — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="contacts">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Contacts — coming soon</p>
      </div>

    {% elif entity == "contacts" %}
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="emails">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Emails — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="phones">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Phones — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="urls">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">URLs — coming soon</p>
      </div>
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="organizations">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Organizations — coming soon</p>
      </div>

    {% elif entity == "organizations" %}
      <div class="detail-tab-panel" data-tab="contacts">
        <p class="tab-placeholder">Contacts — coming soon</p>
      </div>
    {% endif %}

  </div>

  <!-- Action buttons: sticky footer — actions and container_class from route -->
  {% include 'partials/_form_actions.html' %}

</div>
```

### AFTER

```jinja
{#
  _detail_panel.html

  Bare shell for the detail panel — just the outer container div with
  data-entity/data-id attributes for JS to read. Actual content (tab
  bar, form, child tabs, action buttons) lives in
  _detail_panel_content.html, included here for crew.html's initial
  page-load render, and re-rendered wholesale by panel.py on every
  subsequent panel open — see detail-panel.js's fetchAndSwapPanel(),
  which replaces .detail-panel's entire innerHTML with panel.py's
  response.

  Parameters — same as _detail_panel_content.html; passed through
  automatically via Jinja's context-sharing include behavior, not
  restated here.
#}

<div class="detail-panel" data-entity="{{ entity }}" data-id="{{ record_id }}">
  {% include "partials/_detail_panel_content.html" %}
</div>
```

**Why:** This file now only renders once, at initial page load via
`crew.html`. Every subsequent open goes through `panel.py`, which renders
`_detail_panel_content.html` directly (no outer wrapper div — the wrapper
already exists in the DOM and isn't replaced, only its `innerHTML` is).

## `panel.py`

### BEFORE

```python
"""Detail panel field-fragment routes.

Serves a single entity's field-input fragment, rendered via fieldkit,
for detail-panel.js to fetch-and-swap into the form container on every
panel open (new record or existing). Replaces the old approach of one
static per-entity form baked into _detail_panel.html at page load.

Mirrors crew.py's raw jinja2.Environment setup rather than introducing
FastAPI's Jinja2Templates as a second templating convention.
"""

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db
from curator.web.routes.contacts import _fetch_contact_for_display
from curator.web.routes.organizations import _fetch_organization_for_display
from curator.web.routes.projects import _fetch_project_for_display

TEMPLATES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "templates"
env = Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(TEMPLATES_DIR))

router = APIRouter()

# Entity name -> its _fetch_*_for_display function. Small, fixed set of
# wiring decisions, same reasoning as app.py's _FIELDKIT_VIEWS: adding
# an entity means adding routes/templates alongside it regardless, so
# there's no scenario where this changes without a code change too.
_FETCH_FUNCTIONS = {
    "projects": _fetch_project_for_display,
    "contacts": _fetch_contact_for_display,
    "organizations": _fetch_organization_for_display,
}


def _render_fields(request: Request, entity: str, record: dict) -> HTMLResponse:
    """Render the field-fragment template for one entity + record.

    Args:
        request: Current request — used to reach app.state.fieldkit,
                 the FieldKit cache built once at FastAPI startup.
        entity:  One of "projects", "contacts", "organizations".
        record:  Field values dict, or {} for a new record.

    Returns:
        HTMLResponse — the rendered fragment, ready to be swapped into
        #detail-form-fields by detail-panel.js.
    """
    kit = request.app.state.fieldkit[entity]
    template = env.get_template("partials/_detail_form_fields.html")
    return HTMLResponse(
        template.render(fields=kit.fields, record=record, options=kit.options)
    )


# /panel/{entity}/new must be declared before /panel/{entity}/{record_id}
# — same route-ordering rule as the save routes (literal before
# parameterized), otherwise FastAPI tries to parse "new" as an int and
# 422s instead of matching this route.

@router.get("/panel/{entity}/new")
async def panel_new(entity: str, request: Request):
    """Render the field fragment for a new, empty record."""
    if entity not in _FETCH_FUNCTIONS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown entity: {entity}")
    return _render_fields(request, entity, {})


@router.get("/panel/{entity}/{record_id}")
async def panel_existing(
    entity: str,
    record_id: int,
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Render the field fragment for an existing record."""
    if entity not in _FETCH_FUNCTIONS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown entity: {entity}")

    fetch_fn = _FETCH_FUNCTIONS[entity]
    record = await fetch_fn(db, record_id)
    if not record:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"{entity.title()} not found")

    return _render_fields(request, entity, record)
```

### AFTER

```python
"""Detail panel content routes.

Serves a single entity's full panel content (tab bar, fieldkit-driven
form, child-tab placeholders, action buttons), rendered via
_detail_panel_content.html, for detail-panel.js to fetch-and-swap into
.detail-panel on every panel open (new record or existing).

Previously rendered only _detail_form_fields.html — the bare field
<div>s, no tab bar or form wrapper — which silently wiped out the tab
bar on every open, since detail-panel.js replaces .detail-panel's
entire innerHTML. Fixed by rendering the same content template
_detail_panel.html now delegates to for its own initial-page-load
render. See CHANGEDOC_DETAIL_PANEL_CONTENT_SPLIT.md for the full
diagnosis.

Mirrors crew.py's raw jinja2.Environment setup rather than introducing
FastAPI's Jinja2Templates as a second templating convention.
"""

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.formkit import FormActions
from curator.web.deps import get_db
from curator.web.routes.contacts import _fetch_contact_for_display
from curator.web.routes.organizations import _fetch_organization_for_display
from curator.web.routes.projects import _fetch_project_for_display

TEMPLATES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "templates"
_FORMS_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "data" / "forms.yaml"
env = Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(TEMPLATES_DIR))

router = APIRouter()

# Entity name -> its _fetch_*_for_display function. Small, fixed set of
# wiring decisions, same reasoning as app.py's _FIELDKIT_VIEWS: adding
# an entity means adding routes/templates alongside it regardless, so
# there's no scenario where this changes without a code change too.
_FETCH_FUNCTIONS = {
    "projects": _fetch_project_for_display,
    "contacts": _fetch_contact_for_display,
    "organizations": _fetch_organization_for_display,
}


def _render_panel_content(
    request: Request, entity: str, record: dict, record_id
) -> HTMLResponse:
    """Render the full panel-content template for one entity + record.

    Args:
        request:   Current request — used to reach app.state.fieldkit,
                   the FieldKit cache built once at FastAPI startup.
        entity:    One of "projects", "contacts", "organizations".
        record:    Field values dict, or {} for a new record.
        record_id: The record's id, or '' for a new record — set on
                   the <form> and <div class="detail-panel"> data
                   attributes JS reads.

    Returns:
        HTMLResponse — the rendered content (tab bar, form, child-tab
        placeholders, action buttons), ready to be swapped into
        .detail-panel's innerHTML by detail-panel.js.
    """
    kit = request.app.state.fieldkit[entity]
    detail_panel_actions = FormActions.from_yaml(_FORMS_PATH, "detail_panel")
    template = env.get_template("partials/_detail_panel_content.html")
    return HTMLResponse(
        template.render(
            entity=entity,
            record_id=record_id,
            record=record,
            fields=kit.fields,
            options=kit.options,
            actions=detail_panel_actions["actions"],
            container_class=detail_panel_actions["container_class"],
        )
    )


# /panel/{entity}/new must be declared before /panel/{entity}/{record_id}
# — same route-ordering rule as the save routes (literal before
# parameterized), otherwise FastAPI tries to parse "new" as an int and
# 422s instead of matching this route.

@router.get("/panel/{entity}/new")
async def panel_new(entity: str, request: Request):
    """Render the full panel content for a new, empty record."""
    if entity not in _FETCH_FUNCTIONS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown entity: {entity}")
    return _render_panel_content(request, entity, {}, "")


@router.get("/panel/{entity}/{record_id}")
async def panel_existing(
    entity: str,
    record_id: int,
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Render the full panel content for an existing record."""
    if entity not in _FETCH_FUNCTIONS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown entity: {entity}")

    fetch_fn = _FETCH_FUNCTIONS[entity]
    record = await fetch_fn(db, record_id)
    if not record:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"{entity.title()} not found")

    return _render_panel_content(request, entity, record, record_id)
```

**Why:** `_render_fields` is renamed `_render_panel_content` since it now
renders considerably more than fields — the old name would be misleading.
`record_id` is now threaded through explicitly (previously absent — the old
field-only fragment didn't need it, but the `<form>`/`<div class="detail-panel">`
data attributes inside the content template do).

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_TASKS_SQL_LAYER

# Changedoc: Tasks SQL Layer

**Date:** 2026-07-06
**Depends on:** `03_projects.sql`, `07_detail_views.sql`, `07_detail_api.sql`,
`06b_api_projects.sql`, `08b_api_lookup.sql` (all as uploaded this session)

**Scope:** Database layer only. This is step 1 of wiring Tasks into the UI —
`v_task_detail`, `api.get_task_detail()`, `api.save_task()`,
`api.delete_task()`, two new `api.get_lookup()` branches, and dropping
`projects.tasks.sort_order`. Python/fieldkit/template work follows once this
is verified in pgAdmin.

**Decisions this reflects (confirmed with Carolyn):**
- `project_id` is a hidden, pre-filled field on the task form (fieldkit change,
  not part of this changedoc — noted at the bottom).
- Subtasks (`parent_id`) are in scope. A parent task must belong to the same
  project; a task can't be its own parent. Deeper cycle detection
  (grandparent loops) is **not** implemented — flagged as a known gap below.
- `sort_order` is dead weight with no consumer — dropped entirely. Ordering
  is expected to come from naming convention (`01_task`, `02_task`) or
  sorting by name/due-date in the UI, not a stored order column.

---

4. **New save/delete functions** (Section 4)
5. **Updated `get_lookup()`** (Section 5) — full `CREATE OR REPLACE`, safe to

## Section 2 — New view (run this statement only, not the whole file)

```sql
CREATE VIEW projects.v_task_detail AS
SELECT
    id,
    project_id,
    parent_id,
    description,
    notes,
    status_id,
    priority_id
FROM projects.tasks;

GRANT SELECT ON projects.v_task_detail TO steward;
```

`completed_at` is deliberately excluded — same reasoning as `slug` on

```sql
RETURNS JSONB
```

## Section 4 — New save/delete functions

```sql
-- =============================================================================
-- api.save_task(payload JSONB, user_id BIGINT)
--
-- Insert or update a task record.
-- payload.id present and non-null -> UPDATE; absent or null -> INSERT.
--
-- Unlike api.save_project(), status_id and priority_id are taken as ids
-- directly, not name strings -- fieldkit's <select> fields post the id
-- from api.get_lookup(), so there's no name-to-id resolution step needed
-- here the way the older hand-coded project form required.
--
-- completed_at is not accepted from the payload -- it's derived from
-- status_id.is_terminal on every save (stamped NOW() when terminal, cleared
-- when not), matching the project_templates_design.md rule that a task's
-- completed_at reflects its current status, not a preserved timestamp.
--
-- parent_id, if provided, must reference an existing task in the SAME
-- project, and can't be the task's own id. Deeper cycle detection
-- (e.g. a task set as its own grandparent) is not implemented -- flagged
-- as a known gap, not expected to come up with the shallow subtask depth
-- this UI supports.
--
-- Payload shape:
-- {
--   "id":          null,           -- null/absent = INSERT, int = UPDATE
--   "project_id":  12,              -- required
--   "parent_id":   null,            -- optional, must be same project
--   "description": "Fix the latch", -- required
--   "notes":       "...",           -- optional
--   "status_id":   3,               -- required
--   "priority_id": 2                -- optional
-- }
-- =============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION api.save_task(
    p_payload JSONB,
    p_user_id BIGINT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_id                 BIGINT;
    v_project_id         BIGINT;
    v_parent_id          BIGINT;
    v_description        TEXT;
    v_notes              TEXT;
    v_status_id          BIGINT;
    v_priority_id        BIGINT;
    v_is_terminal        BOOLEAN;
    v_completed_at       TIMESTAMPTZ;
    v_is_update          BOOLEAN;
    v_parent_project_id  BIGINT;
BEGIN
    v_description := TRIM(p_payload->>'description');

    IF v_description IS NULL OR v_description = '' THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'Task description is required.'
        );
    END IF;

    v_project_id := (p_payload->>'project_id')::BIGINT;

    IF v_project_id IS NULL THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'A project is required.'
        );
    END IF;

    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects.projects WHERE id = v_project_id) THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'Project not found.'
        );
    END IF;

    v_status_id := (p_payload->>'status_id')::BIGINT;

    IF v_status_id IS NULL THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'Task status is required.'
        );
    END IF;

    SELECT is_terminal INTO v_is_terminal
    FROM projects.task_status
    WHERE id = v_status_id;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'Task status not found.'
        );
    END IF;

    v_priority_id := (p_payload->>'priority_id')::BIGINT;
    v_notes       := NULLIF(TRIM(p_payload->>'notes'), '');
    v_parent_id   := (p_payload->>'parent_id')::BIGINT;
    v_id          := (p_payload->>'id')::BIGINT;
    v_is_update   := v_id IS NOT NULL;

    IF v_parent_id IS NOT NULL THEN
        IF v_is_update AND v_parent_id = v_id THEN
            RETURN jsonb_build_object(
                'success', FALSE,
                'data',    NULL,
                'message', 'A task cannot be its own parent.'
            );
        END IF;

        SELECT project_id INTO v_parent_project_id
        FROM projects.tasks
        WHERE id = v_parent_id;

        IF NOT FOUND THEN
            RETURN jsonb_build_object(
                'success', FALSE,
                'data',    NULL,
                'message', 'Parent task not found.'
            );
        END IF;

        IF v_parent_project_id != v_project_id THEN
            RETURN jsonb_build_object(
                'success', FALSE,
                'data',    NULL,
                'message', 'Parent task must belong to the same project.'
            );
        END IF;
    END IF;

    v_completed_at := CASE WHEN v_is_terminal THEN NOW() ELSE NULL END;

    IF v_is_update THEN
        IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects.tasks WHERE id = v_id) THEN
            RETURN jsonb_build_object(
                'success', FALSE,
                'data',    NULL,
                'message', 'Task not found.'
            );
        END IF;

        UPDATE projects.tasks SET
            project_id   = v_project_id,
            parent_id    = v_parent_id,
            description  = v_description,
            notes        = v_notes,
            status_id    = v_status_id,
            priority_id  = v_priority_id,
            completed_at = v_completed_at,
            updated_by   = p_user_id
        WHERE id = v_id;

        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', TRUE,
            'data',    jsonb_build_object('id', v_id),
            'message', 'Task updated.'
        );
    ELSE
        INSERT INTO projects.tasks (
            project_id, parent_id, description, notes,
            status_id, priority_id, completed_at,
            created_by, updated_by
        ) VALUES (
            v_project_id, v_parent_id, v_description, v_notes,
            v_status_id, v_priority_id, v_completed_at,
            p_user_id, p_user_id
        )
        RETURNING id INTO v_id;

        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', TRUE,
            'data',    jsonb_build_object('id', v_id),
            'message', 'Task created.'
        );
    END IF;

EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
    RAISE WARNING 'api.save_task error: %', SQLERRM;
    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'success', FALSE,
        'data',    NULL,
        'message', 'An unexpected error occurred saving the task.'
    );
END;
$$;


-- =============================================================================
-- api.delete_task(id BIGINT, user_id BIGINT)
--
-- Hard delete. parent_id is ON DELETE NO ACTION (03_projects.sql), so a task
-- with subtasks can't be deleted out from under them -- checked explicitly
-- for a clear message, with the foreign_key_violation catch kept as a
-- fallback for any other dependent-record case.
-- =============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION api.delete_task(
    p_id      BIGINT,
    p_user_id BIGINT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects.tasks WHERE id = p_id) THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'Task not found.'
        );
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects.tasks WHERE parent_id = p_id) THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'Cannot delete task — it has subtasks. Delete or reassign them first.'
        );
    END IF;

    DELETE FROM projects.tasks WHERE id = p_id;

    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'success', TRUE,
        'data',    jsonb_build_object('id', p_id),
        'message', 'Task deleted.'
    );

EXCEPTION WHEN foreign_key_violation THEN
    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'success', FALSE,
        'data',    NULL,
        'message', 'Cannot delete task — it has dependent records.'
    );
WHEN OTHERS THEN
    RAISE WARNING 'api.delete_task error for id %: %', p_id, SQLERRM;
    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'success', FALSE,
        'data',    NULL,
        'message', 'An unexpected error occurred deleting the task.'
    );
END;
$$;
```

---

## Section 5 — Updated `get_lookup()` (full replace, safe to rerun)

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION api.get_lookup(p_source TEXT)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_result JSONB;
BEGIN
    CASE p_source
        WHEN 'project_types' THEN
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                       jsonb_build_object('value', id, 'label', name)
                       ORDER BY name
                   )
            INTO v_result
            FROM projects.project_type;

        WHEN 'project_statuses' THEN
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                       jsonb_build_object('value', id, 'label', name)
                       ORDER BY name
                   )
            INTO v_result
            FROM projects.project_status;

        WHEN 'task_statuses' THEN
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                       jsonb_build_object('value', id, 'label', name)
                       ORDER BY name
                   )
            INTO v_result
            FROM projects.task_status;

        WHEN 'priorities' THEN
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                       jsonb_build_object('value', id, 'label', name)
                       ORDER BY name
                   )
            INTO v_result
            FROM projects.priority;

        ELSE
            v_result := NULL;
    END CASE;

    RETURN v_result;
END;
$$;
```

## `06b_api_projects.sql`

### BEFORE

*(unchanged from the version you uploaded — full file below for reference,
diff is purely additive after `api.delete_project`)*

```sql
-- =============================================================================
-- 06b_api_projects.sql — API schema: projects.* stored procedures
-- =============================================================================
--
-- Split from 06_api.sql — paired with 03_projects.sql (the schema these
-- procs operate on). A future database reusing 03_projects.sql's schema
-- can also reuse this file without dragging along auth or identity procs.
--
-- All procs SECURITY DEFINER — see 06a_api_auth.sql header for the full
-- security model note (applies to all api.* files, not repeated per file).
--
-- Depends on: 01_audit.sql, 03_projects.sql
-- GRANTs live in 06d_api_grants.sql.
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- api.save_project(payload JSONB, user_id BIGINT)
--
-- Insert or update a project record.
-- payload.id present and non-null → UPDATE; absent or null → INSERT.
--
-- Handles:
--   - Slug generation from name (lowercase, spaces to hyphens, deduplication)
--   - status_id and type_id lookup by name if provided as strings
--   - created_by / updated_by stamping
--   - Conflict detection (duplicate name)
--
-- Payload shape:
-- {
--   "id":          null,           -- null/absent = INSERT, int = UPDATE
--   "name":        "My Project",   -- required
--   "description": "...",          -- optional
--   "notes":       "...",          -- optional
--   "status":      "active",       -- name string, looked up to id
--   "type":        "coding",       -- name string, looked up to id (nullable)
--   "target_date": "2026-12-31"    -- ISO date string (nullable)
-- }
-- =============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION api.save_project(
    p_payload JSONB,
    p_user_id BIGINT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_id          BIGINT;
    v_name        VARCHAR(255);
    v_slug        VARCHAR(100);
    v_slug_base   VARCHAR(100);
    v_slug_suffix INT := 0;
    v_description TEXT;
    v_notes       TEXT;
    v_status_id   BIGINT;
    v_type_id     BIGINT;
    v_target_date DATE;
    v_is_update   BOOLEAN;
BEGIN
    v_name := TRIM(p_payload->>'name');

    IF v_name IS NULL OR v_name = '' THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'Project name is required.'
        );
    END IF;

    v_id        := (p_payload->>'id')::BIGINT;
    v_is_update := v_id IS NOT NULL;

    v_description := NULLIF(TRIM(p_payload->>'description'), '');
    v_notes       := NULLIF(TRIM(p_payload->>'notes'), '');
    v_target_date := NULLIF(p_payload->>'target_date', '')::DATE;

    SELECT id INTO v_status_id
    FROM projects.project_status
    WHERE name = LOWER(TRIM(p_payload->>'status'));

    IF v_status_id IS NULL THEN
        SELECT id INTO v_status_id
        FROM projects.project_status
        WHERE name = 'active';
    END IF;

    IF p_payload->>'type' IS NOT NULL AND p_payload->>'type' != '' THEN
        SELECT id INTO v_type_id
        FROM projects.project_type
        WHERE name = LOWER(TRIM(p_payload->>'type'));
    END IF;

    IF v_is_update THEN
        IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects.projects WHERE id = v_id) THEN
            RETURN jsonb_build_object(
                'success', FALSE,
                'data',    NULL,
                'message', 'Project not found.'
            );
        END IF;

        IF EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM projects.projects
            WHERE name = v_name AND id != v_id
        ) THEN
            RETURN jsonb_build_object(
                'success', FALSE,
                'data',    NULL,
                'message', 'A project with that name already exists.'
            );
        END IF;

        UPDATE projects.projects SET
            name        = v_name,
            description = v_description,
            notes       = v_notes,
            status_id   = v_status_id,
            type_id     = v_type_id,
            target_date = v_target_date,
            updated_by  = p_user_id
        WHERE id = v_id;

        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', TRUE,
            'data',    jsonb_build_object('id', v_id),
            'message', 'Project updated.'
        );

    ELSE
        IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects.projects WHERE name = v_name) THEN
            RETURN jsonb_build_object(
                'success', FALSE,
                'data',    NULL,
                'message', 'A project with that name already exists.'
            );
        END IF;

        v_slug_base := LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(
            REGEXP_REPLACE(v_name, '[^a-zA-Z0-9\s-]', '', 'g'),
            '\s+', '-', 'g'
        ));
        v_slug_base := TRIM(BOTH '-' FROM v_slug_base);
        v_slug      := v_slug_base;

        WHILE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects.projects WHERE slug = v_slug) LOOP
            v_slug_suffix := v_slug_suffix + 1;
            v_slug := v_slug_base || '-' || v_slug_suffix;
        END LOOP;

        INSERT INTO projects.projects (
            name, slug, description, notes,
            status_id, type_id, target_date,
            created_by, updated_by
        ) VALUES (
            v_name, v_slug, v_description, v_notes,
            v_status_id, v_type_id, v_target_date,
            p_user_id, p_user_id
        )
        RETURNING id INTO v_id;

        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', TRUE,
            'data',    jsonb_build_object('id', v_id, 'slug', v_slug),
            'message', 'Project created.'
        );
    END IF;

EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
    RAISE WARNING 'api.save_project error: %', SQLERRM;
    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'success', FALSE,
        'data',    NULL,
        'message', 'An unexpected error occurred saving the project.'
    );
END;
$$;


-- =============================================================================
-- api.delete_project(id BIGINT, user_id BIGINT)
--
-- Soft-deletes are not implemented yet — this is a hard delete.
-- Audit trigger on projects.projects captures the DELETE for the log.
-- Returns error if project has dependent records that block deletion.
-- =============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION api.delete_project(
    p_id      BIGINT,
    p_user_id BIGINT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects.projects WHERE id = p_id) THEN
        RETURN jsonb_build_object(
            'success', FALSE,
            'data',    NULL,
            'message', 'Project not found.'
        );
    END IF;

    DELETE FROM projects.projects WHERE id = p_id;

    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'success', TRUE,
        'data',    jsonb_build_object('id', p_id),
        'message', 'Project deleted.'
    );

EXCEPTION WHEN foreign_key_violation THEN
    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'success', FALSE,
        'data',    NULL,
        'message', 'Cannot delete project — it has dependent records.'
    );
WHEN OTHERS THEN
    RAISE WARNING 'api.delete_project error for id %: %', p_id, SQLERRM;
    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
        'success', FALSE,
        'data',    NULL,
        'message', 'An unexpected error occurred deleting the project.'
    );
END;
$$;
```

### AFTER

Everything above stays identical, with `api.save_task()` and
`api.delete_task()` (full text in Section 4) appended at the end of the file.

**Why here:** `06b_api_projects.sql` is paired with `03_projects.sql`, which
contains both `projects.projects` and `projects.tasks` — same schema-pairing
convention that put `save_project`/`delete_project` here in the first place.

## 2. `src/curator/static/js/bidirectional-filter.js` (edit — complete file)

**What changed:** accepts a new `detailBtnId` config key, shows/hides
and populates that button's entity/id whenever selection changes, and
wires its click to `window.openDetailPanel` — the same call the
(unreliable) `dblclick` handler already makes. The `dblclick` handler
itself is left in place, untouched — no harm in keeping it, and it may
simply start working reliably on its own another day; this changedoc
doesn't chase that question further.

### BEFORE (complete file, as uploaded)

```javascript
/**
 * bidirectional-filter.js
 *
 * Reusable two-listbox cross-filter pattern: two lists of records connected
 * by a relationship (many-to-many or one-to-many). Selecting an item in
 * either list filters the other to only related items. A shared selection
 * readout shows whichever item was last clicked. Double-click opens that
 * record's detail panel; each list has its own live-search input and an
 * "add new" button.
 *
 * Not specific to any entity pair — first consumer is Organizations ↔
 * Contacts (Identities tab), but this is written generically enough for
 * any two-list cross-reference UI (e.g. a future Projects ↔ Contacts tab).
 *
 * Markup contract for each list item:
 *   <div class="identity-item"
 *        data-id="123"
 *        data-name="Display Name"
 *        data-related-ids="4,7,9">
 *
 * data-related-ids holds the comma-separated ids of items in the *other*
 * list that this item is connected to. Both sides use the same attribute
 * name — the module doesn't care which side is "left" or "right".
 *
 * Depends on: window.openDetailPanel, window.openNewRecordPanel
 * (both exposed globally by detail-panel.js).
 *
 * Usage:
 *   import { initBidirectionalFilter } from './bidirectional-filter.js';
 *
 *   initBidirectionalFilter({
 *     selectionBoxId: 'identity-selection',
 *     left: {
 *       listboxId: 'org-listbox',
 *       searchId:  'org-search',
 *       addBtnId:  'org-add-btn',
 *       entity:    'organizations',
 *     },
 *     right: {
 *       listboxId: 'contact-listbox',
 *       searchId:  'contact-search',
 *       addBtnId:  'contact-add-btn',
 *       entity:    'contacts',
 *     },
 *   });
 */

/**
 * @param {Object} config
 * @param {string} config.selectionBoxId - id of the shared selection readout element
 * @param {Object} config.left  - { listboxId, searchId, addBtnId, entity }
 * @param {Object} config.right - { listboxId, searchId, addBtnId, entity }
 */
export function initBidirectionalFilter(config) {
  const { selectionBoxId, left, right } = config;

  const selectionBox = document.getElementById(selectionBoxId);

  function makeSide(side, other) {
    return {
      listbox: document.getElementById(side.listboxId),
      search:  document.getElementById(side.searchId),
      addBtn:  document.getElementById(side.addBtnId),
      entity:  side.entity,
      selectedId: null,
      // set after both sides constructed — see wiring below
      other: null,
    };
  }

  const leftSide  = makeSide(left, right);
  const rightSide = makeSide(right, left);
  leftSide.other  = rightSide;
  rightSide.other = leftSide;

  function getItems(side) {
    return side.listbox.querySelectorAll('.identity-item');
  }

  function setItemVisible(el, visible) {
    el.style.display = visible ? '' : 'none';
  }

  function showSelection(name) {
    selectionBox.textContent = name;
    selectionBox.classList.add('has-selection');
  }

  function clearSelectionBox() {
    selectionBox.innerHTML = '<span class="identity-selection-placeholder">No selection</span>';
    selectionBox.classList.remove('has-selection');
  }

  function selectItem(side, item) {
    getItems(side).forEach(i => i.classList.remove('selected'));
    side.selectedId = item.dataset.id;
    item.classList.add('selected');
    showSelection(item.dataset.name);

    const relatedIds = item.dataset.relatedIds
      ? item.dataset.relatedIds.split(',').filter(Boolean)
      : [];
    getItems(side.other).forEach(o => {
      setItemVisible(o, relatedIds.includes(o.dataset.id));
    });

    side.other.selectedId = null;
    getItems(side.other).forEach(i => i.classList.remove('selected'));
  }

  function clearSelection(side) {
    side.selectedId = null;
    clearSelectionBox();
    getItems(side).forEach(i => {
      i.classList.remove('selected');
      setItemVisible(i, true);
    });
    applySearch(side.other);
  }

  function applySearch(side) {
    const term = side.search.value.toLowerCase();
    getItems(side).forEach(item => {
      setItemVisible(item, item.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(term));
    });
  }

  function wireSide(side) {
    side.listbox.addEventListener('click', e => {
      const item = e.target.closest('.identity-item');
      if (!item) return;
      if (item.dataset.id === side.selectedId) {
        clearSelection(side);
      } else {
        selectItem(side, item);
      }
    });

    side.listbox.addEventListener('dblclick', e => {
      const item = e.target.closest('.identity-item');
      if (!item) return;
      window.openDetailPanel(side.entity, item.dataset.id);
    });

    side.search.addEventListener('input', () => {
      if (side.selectedId) clearSelection(side);
      applySearch(side);
    });

    if (side.addBtn) {
      side.addBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        window.openNewRecordPanel(side.entity);
      });
    }
  }

  wireSide(leftSide);
  wireSide(rightSide);
}
```

```javascript
/**
 * bidirectional-filter.js
 *
 * Reusable two-listbox cross-filter pattern: two lists of records connected
 * by a relationship (many-to-many or one-to-many). Selecting an item in
 * either list filters the other to only related items. A shared selection
 * readout shows whichever item was last clicked, alongside a ⋯ button
 * (same detail-icon pattern as the Projects datasheet) to open that
 * item's detail panel. Double-click also attempts to open it directly —
 * that handler is wired correctly but hasn't proven reliable in
 * practice; the ⋯ button is the dependable path and doesn't require
 * chasing that down. Each list has its own live-search input and an
 * "add new" button.
 *
 * Not specific to any entity pair — first consumer is Organizations ↔
 * Contacts (Identities tab), but this is written generically enough for
 * any two-list cross-reference UI (e.g. a future Projects ↔ Contacts tab).
 *
 * Markup contract for each list item:
 *   <div class="identity-item"
 *        data-id="123"
 *        data-name="Display Name"
 *        data-related-ids="4,7,9">
 *
 * data-related-ids holds the comma-separated ids of items in the *other*
 * list that this item is connected to. Both sides use the same attribute
 * name — the module doesn't care which side is "left" or "right".
 *
 * Depends on: window.openDetailPanel, window.openNewRecordPanel
 * (both exposed globally by detail-panel.js).
 *
 * Usage:
 *   import { initBidirectionalFilter } from './bidirectional-filter.js';
 *
 *   initBidirectionalFilter({
 *     selectionBoxId: 'identity-selection',
 *     detailBtnId:    'identity-detail-btn',
 *     left: {
 *       listboxId: 'org-listbox',
 *       searchId:  'org-search',
 *       addBtnId:  'org-add-btn',
 *       entity:    'organizations',
 *     },
 *     right: {
 *       listboxId: 'contact-listbox',
 *       searchId:  'contact-search',
 *       addBtnId:  'contact-add-btn',
 *       entity:    'contacts',
 *     },
 *   });
 */

/**
 * @param {Object} config
 * @param {string} config.selectionBoxId - id of the shared selection readout element
 * @param {string} config.detailBtnId - id of the ⋯ button inside the readout
 *   that opens the currently selected item's detail panel
 * @param {Object} config.left  - { listboxId, searchId, addBtnId, entity }
 * @param {Object} config.right - { listboxId, searchId, addBtnId, entity }
 */
export function initBidirectionalFilter(config) {
  const { selectionBoxId, detailBtnId, left, right } = config;

  const selectionBox = document.getElementById(selectionBoxId);
  const detailBtn    = document.getElementById(detailBtnId);

  function makeSide(side, other) {
    return {
      listbox: document.getElementById(side.listboxId),
      search:  document.getElementById(side.searchId),
      addBtn:  document.getElementById(side.addBtnId),
      entity:  side.entity,
      selectedId: null,
      // set after both sides constructed — see wiring below
      other: null,
    };
  }

  const leftSide  = makeSide(left, right);
  const rightSide = makeSide(right, left);
  leftSide.other  = rightSide;
  rightSide.other = leftSide;

  function getItems(side) {
    return side.listbox.querySelectorAll('.identity-item');
  }

  function setItemVisible(el, visible) {
    el.style.display = visible ? '' : 'none';
  }

  function showSelection(name) {
    selectionBox.textContent = name;
    selectionBox.classList.add('has-selection');
    // Re-append here since textContent above wiped detailBtn out of the
    // readout along with the placeholder span — restore it as a sibling.
    if (detailBtn) selectionBox.appendChild(detailBtn);
  }

  function clearSelectionBox() {
    selectionBox.innerHTML = '<span class="identity-selection-placeholder">No selection</span>';
    selectionBox.classList.remove('has-selection');
    // innerHTML above destroys detailBtn's original DOM node along with
    // everything else in the readout — same restoration as showSelection.
    if (detailBtn) {
      detailBtn.style.display = 'none';
      selectionBox.appendChild(detailBtn);
    }
  }

  function selectItem(side, item) {
    getItems(side).forEach(i => i.classList.remove('selected'));
    side.selectedId = item.dataset.id;
    item.classList.add('selected');
    showSelection(item.dataset.name);

    if (detailBtn) {
      detailBtn.dataset.entity = side.entity;
      detailBtn.dataset.id     = item.dataset.id;
      detailBtn.style.display  = '';
    }

    const relatedIds = item.dataset.relatedIds
      ? item.dataset.relatedIds.split(',').filter(Boolean)
      : [];
    getItems(side.other).forEach(o => {
      setItemVisible(o, relatedIds.includes(o.dataset.id));
    });

    side.other.selectedId = null;
    getItems(side.other).forEach(i => i.classList.remove('selected'));
  }

  function clearSelection(side) {
    side.selectedId = null;
    clearSelectionBox();
    getItems(side).forEach(i => {
      i.classList.remove('selected');
      setItemVisible(i, true);
    });
    applySearch(side.other);
  }

  function applySearch(side) {
    const term = side.search.value.toLowerCase();
    getItems(side).forEach(item => {
      setItemVisible(item, item.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(term));
    });
  }

  function wireSide(side) {
    side.listbox.addEventListener('click', e => {
      const item = e.target.closest('.identity-item');
      if (!item) return;
      if (item.dataset.id === side.selectedId) {
        clearSelection(side);
      } else {
        selectItem(side, item);
      }
    });

    side.listbox.addEventListener('dblclick', e => {
      const item = e.target.closest('.identity-item');
      if (!item) return;
      window.openDetailPanel(side.entity, item.dataset.id);
    });

    side.search.addEventListener('input', () => {
      if (side.selectedId) clearSelection(side);
      applySearch(side);
    });

    if (side.addBtn) {
      side.addBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        window.openNewRecordPanel(side.entity);
      });
    }
  }

  if (detailBtn) {
    detailBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
      const { entity, id } = detailBtn.dataset;
      if (entity && id) window.openDetailPanel(entity, id);
    });
  }

  wireSide(leftSide);
  wireSide(rightSide);
}
```

**Why `showSelection`/`clearSelectionBox` re-append `detailBtn`:** both
functions replace the readout's contents wholesale
(`textContent = ...` / `innerHTML = ...`), which would destroy the
button's DOM node (and its click listener) along with the placeholder
text it's replacing. Re-appending the same node after each replacement
keeps the one listener attached at init working indefinitely, rather
than needing to re-wire a click handler every time selection changes.

## 📄 detail-panel.js

/**
 * detail-panel.js
 *
 * Handles detail panel interactions:
 * - Opening detail panel for existing records (⋯ button)
 * - Opening detail panel for new records (+ Add button)
 * - Closing panel on × / Alt+X / Escape
 * - Tab switching
 * - Save (Alt+S) — save and close
 * - New  (Alt+N) — save current, clear form, focus Name
 * - Discard (Alt+X) — discard and close
 *
 * Hero image and detail panel occupy the same spot. Opening the panel
 * hides the hero (display:none) and shows the panel (display:flex).
 *
 * Field rendering is fetch-and-swap: opening a record fetches the
 * whole panel body — tab bar, form, everything — from
 * /panel/{entity}/{id} (or /panel/{entity}/new), built by fieldkit from
 * the entity's actual schema, and swaps it into .detail-panel wholesale.
 * There is no client-side knowledge of what fields or tabs any entity
 * has; adding a new entity requires no JS change.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Internal helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function getPanel() {
  return document.querySelector('#detail-panel-container .detail-panel');
}

function getForm() {
  return document.getElementById('detail-form');
}

function getHero() {
  return document.querySelector('.crew-header');
}

function showPanel() {
  const panel = getPanel();
  const hero  = getHero();
  if (panel) panel.classList.add('active');
  if (hero)  hero.classList.add('hidden');
}

function hidePanel() {
  const panel = getPanel();
  const hero  = getHero();
  if (panel) panel.classList.remove('active');
  if (hero)  hero.classList.remove('hidden');
}

function resetToDetailsTab() {
  const panel = getPanel();
  if (!panel) return;
  panel.querySelectorAll('.detail-tab-button').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
  panel.querySelectorAll('.detail-tab-panel').forEach(p => p.classList.remove('active'));
  const firstBtn   = panel.querySelector('.detail-tab-button');
  const detailsTab = panel.querySelector('.detail-tab-panel[data-tab="details"]');
  if (firstBtn)   firstBtn.classList.add('active');
  if (detailsTab) detailsTab.classList.add('active');
}

function clearForm() {
  const form = getForm();
  if (!form) return;
  form.dataset.id = '';
  form.querySelectorAll('input, textarea').forEach(el => el.value = '');
  form.querySelectorAll('select').forEach(el => el.selectedIndex = 0);
}

function focusName() {
  const nameField = document.getElementById('detail-name');
  if (nameField) {
    nameField.focus();
    nameField.select();
  }
}

/**
 * Fetch the full panel body HTML for one entity + record (or 'new')
 * and swap it into .detail-panel — tab bar, form, everything. Swapping
 * the whole thing (not just the field inputs) is what lets opening a
 * different entity show the *right* tab set (e.g. contacts' Emails/
 * Phones/URLs/Organizations, not projects' Tasks/Links/Contacts left
 * over from whatever entity the page originally rendered with).
 *
 * Returns true on success, false on failure (network error, 404 —
 * caller decides whether to proceed with showing the panel).
 */
async function fetchAndSwapPanel(entity, recordIdOrNew) {
  const panel = getPanel();
  if (!panel) return false;

  try {
    const res = await fetch(`/panel/${entity}/${recordIdOrNew}`);
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
    panel.innerHTML = await res.text();
    return true;
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Could not fetch panel content:', err);
    return false;
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Save to server
// Returns the saved record on success, null on failure.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Guard against double-saves from rapid clicks or accesskey + click firing together
let _saving = false;

async function saveForm() {
  const form = getForm();
  if (!form) return null;

  const entity   = form.dataset.entity;
  const recordId = form.dataset.id;
  const isNew    = !recordId;

  const formData = new FormData(form);
  const data     = Object.fromEntries(formData);

  const url = isNew
    ? `/crew/${entity}/save`
    : `/crew/${entity}/${recordId}/save`;

  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(data),
    });

    if (res.ok) {
      const saved = await res.json();
      // Update form id to the newly saved record's id
      form.dataset.id = saved.id;
      const panel = getPanel();
      if (panel) panel.dataset.id = saved.id;
      return saved;
    } else {
      // crew.py returns {"success": false, "message": "..."} on proc
      // rejection (duplicate name, not found, etc.) — read message, not
      // detail, or this always falls back to the generic string below.
      const err = await res.json().catch(() => ({ message: res.statusText }));
      alert(err.message || 'Save failed');
      return null;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Save error:', err);
    alert('Save error: ' + err.message);
    return null;
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Button handlers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function handleSave() {
  if (_saving) return;
  _saving = true;
  try {
    const saved = await saveForm();
    if (saved) {
      if (window._refreshProjectsGrid) window._refreshProjectsGrid();
      hidePanel();
    }
  } finally {
    _saving = false;
  }
}

async function handleNew() {
  if (_saving) return;
  _saving = true;
  try {
    const saved = await saveForm();
    if (!saved) return;
    clearForm();
    resetToDetailsTab();
    focusName();
    if (window._refreshProjectsGrid) window._refreshProjectsGrid();
  } finally {
    _saving = false;
  }
}

function handleDiscard() {
  hidePanel();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public API
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Open detail panel for an existing record.
 * Fetches the whole panel body from /panel/{entity}/{id} and swaps it
 * in wholesale — tab bar included — rather than fetching JSON and
 * manually populating known field names.
 */
export async function openDetailPanel(entity, recordId) {
  const panel = getPanel();
  if (!panel) return;

  const ok = await fetchAndSwapPanel(entity, recordId);
  if (!ok) return;

  panel.dataset.entity = entity;
  panel.dataset.id     = recordId;

  const form = getForm();
  if (form) {
    form.dataset.entity = entity;
    form.dataset.id     = recordId;
  }

  resetToDetailsTab();
  showPanel();
}

/**
 * Open detail panel in new-record mode.
 * Fetches the whole panel body from /panel/{entity}/new (empty values)
 * and swaps it in. Save will POST to /crew/{entity}/save.
 */
export async function openNewRecordPanel(entity) {
  const panel = getPanel();
  if (!panel) return;

  const ok = await fetchAndSwapPanel(entity, 'new');
  if (!ok) return;

  panel.dataset.entity = entity;
  panel.dataset.id     = '';

  const form = getForm();
  if (form) {
    form.dataset.entity = entity;
    form.dataset.id     = '';
  }

  resetToDetailsTab();
  showPanel();
  focusName();
}

/**
 * Close the detail panel and restore the hero image.
 */
export function closeDetailPanel() {
  hidePanel();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Init — wire up all event listeners
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export function initDetailPanel() {
  // Tab switching
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    if (e.target.classList.contains('detail-tab-button')) {
      const panel = e.target.closest('.detail-panel');
      if (!panel) return;
      const targetTab = e.target.dataset.tab;
      panel.querySelectorAll('.detail-tab-button').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
      panel.querySelectorAll('.detail-tab-panel').forEach(p => p.classList.remove('active'));
      e.target.classList.add('active');
      const tabPanel = panel.querySelector(`.detail-tab-panel[data-tab="${targetTab}"]`);
      if (tabPanel) tabPanel.classList.add('active');
    }

    if (e.target.classList.contains('detail-close-button')) handleDiscard();

    // btn-save is type="submit" with form="detail-form" (see forms.yaml) so
    // clicking it also triggers native form submission. Without preventDefault
    // here, the browser's native GET-to-current-URL submission races the
    // fetch() in handleSave() and wins, since nothing else stops it.
    if (e.target.classList.contains('btn-save')) {
      e.preventDefault();
      handleSave();
    }
    if (e.target.classList.contains('btn-new'))             handleNew();
    if (e.target.classList.contains('btn-discard'))         handleDiscard();
  });

  // Keyboard shortcuts
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    const panel = getPanel();
    if (!panel?.classList.contains('active')) return;

    // Alt+S — Save and close
    if (e.altKey && e.key === 's') { e.preventDefault(); handleSave(); }
    // Alt+N — Save and new
    if (e.altKey && e.key === 'n') { e.preventDefault(); handleNew(); }
    // Alt+X or Escape — Discard and close
    if ((e.altKey && e.key === 'x') || e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); handleDiscard(); }
  });

  // Safety net: catch any native form submission (e.g. pressing Enter in a
  // text input, which submits the nearest form by default browser behavior)
  // that isn't already intercepted by the btn-save click handler above.
  // Without this, Enter-to-submit falls back to a GET on the current URL
  // with form fields as query params, identical to the btn-save race bug.
  document.addEventListener('submit', (e) => {
    if (e.target.id === 'detail-form') {
      e.preventDefault();
      handleSave();
    }
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Expose for non-module scripts (e.g. _projects_table.html)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
window.openDetailPanel    = openDetailPanel;
window.openNewRecordPanel = openNewRecordPanel;
window.closeDetailPanel   = closeDetailPanel;

// Initialize
if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initDetailPanel);
} else {
  initDetailPanel();
}

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_FIELDKIT_OPTIONS_AND_FRAGMENT_TEMPLATE

# Changedoc: `FieldKit` caches select options + new field-fragment template

**Date:** 2026-07-04
**Reason:** First two pieces of fetch-and-swap. `FieldKit` already
validates every declared `source:` resolves via `api.get_lookup()`
(previous changedoc) — this reuses that same call to cache the actual
*options*, so the render step never needs its own `get_lookup()` call
per request. The new template is the actual field-rendering logic that
replaces `_detail_panel.html`'s hardcoded per-entity blocks.

**Not yet included in this changedoc:** the `/panel/{entity}/{id}` route
and the `_detail_panel.html`/`detail-panel.js` wiring — those need
`crew.py`'s existing `Jinja2Templates` setup verified first (see note
at the end).

---

## 1. `src/curator/web/fieldkit.py` (edit)

**Design note:** `_validate_sources` already confirmed every source
resolves to something non-empty. `_load_options` reuses that same
`get_lookup()` call to actually cache the result — kept as a separate
method rather than merged into `_validate_sources` to avoid touching
that method's already-tested contract (its existing tests assert only
on raising behavior, not on any return value). The tradeoff: a source
used by more than one field only gets queried once here (deduplicated
by source name), but the *same* source does get queried twice overall
across `_validate_sources` + `_load_options` — a small, deliberate
redundancy at startup only, not per-request, traded for not disturbing
already-verified code.

### BEFORE

```python
    def __init__(self, view_name: str, fields: list[FieldDef]):
        self.view_name = view_name
        self.fields = fields

    @classmethod
    async def create(
        cls,
        db: AsyncDBConnection,
        view_name: str,
        overrides_path: Optional[Path] = None,
    ) -> "FieldKit":
        """
        Build a FieldKit for a single schema-qualified view.

        Args:
            db:             Open AsyncDBConnection.
            view_name:      Schema-qualified view name, e.g.
                            'projects.v_project_detail'.
            overrides_path: Explicit override file path — bypasses the
                            shipped-default/user-override resolution
                            entirely. Intended for tests; leave None in
                            application code.

        Returns:
            Populated FieldKit, fields in view column order.

        Raises:
            FieldSchemaError: If the view has no columns (bad or
                              misspelled view name), or any *_id /
                              integer column has no matching override.
        """
        columns = await cls._fetch_schema(db, view_name)
        if not columns:
            raise FieldSchemaError(
                f"api.get_field_schema('{view_name}') returned no "
                f"columns. Check the view name is correct and "
                f"schema-qualified, e.g. 'projects.v_project_detail'."
            )

        overrides = cls._load_overrides(overrides_path)
        entity_overrides = overrides.get(view_name, {})

        fields = [
            cls._build_field(view_name, column, entity_overrides)
            for column in columns
            if column["name"] != "id"
        ]

        await cls._validate_sources(db, view_name, fields)

        return cls(view_name, fields)
```

### AFTER

```python
    def __init__(
        self,
        view_name: str,
        fields: list[FieldDef],
        options: Optional[dict] = None,
    ):
        self.view_name = view_name
        self.fields = fields
        self.options = options or {}

    @classmethod
    async def create(
        cls,
        db: AsyncDBConnection,
        view_name: str,
        overrides_path: Optional[Path] = None,
    ) -> "FieldKit":
        """
        Build a FieldKit for a single schema-qualified view.

        Args:
            db:             Open AsyncDBConnection.
            view_name:      Schema-qualified view name, e.g.
                            'projects.v_project_detail'.
            overrides_path: Explicit override file path — bypasses the
                            shipped-default/user-override resolution
                            entirely. Intended for tests; leave None in
                            application code.

        Returns:
            Populated FieldKit, fields in view column order, options
            cached per source name for select fields.

        Raises:
            FieldSchemaError: If the view has no columns (bad or
                              misspelled view name), any *_id /
                              integer column has no matching override,
                              or any declared source doesn't resolve.
        """
        columns = await cls._fetch_schema(db, view_name)
        if not columns:
            raise FieldSchemaError(
                f"api.get_field_schema('{view_name}') returned no "
                f"columns. Check the view name is correct and "
                f"schema-qualified, e.g. 'projects.v_project_detail'."
            )

        overrides = cls._load_overrides(overrides_path)
        entity_overrides = overrides.get(view_name, {})

        fields = [
            cls._build_field(view_name, column, entity_overrides)
            for column in columns
            if column["name"] != "id"
        ]

        await cls._validate_sources(db, view_name, fields)
        options = await cls._load_options(db, fields)

        return cls(view_name, fields, options)
```

**New method, added after `_validate_sources`:**

```python
    @staticmethod
    async def _load_options(
        db: AsyncDBConnection, fields: list[FieldDef]
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Fetch and cache select-field options, keyed by source name.

        Called after _validate_sources, which already confirmed every
        declared source resolves to something non-empty — this collects
        those results once at startup so the render step never needs
        its own get_lookup() call per request.

        Args:
            db:     Open connection.
            fields: The FieldDef list already built and validated.

        Returns:
            Dict of source name -> options list (each option a
            {"value": ..., "label": ...} dict, per api.get_lookup()'s
            return shape). Fields with no source contribute nothing;
            two fields sharing the same source only trigger one
            get_lookup() call here.
        """
        options = {}
        for field in fields:
            if field.source is None or field.source in options:
                continue
            options[field.source] = await _fetch_json_scalar(
                db, "SELECT api.get_lookup(%s)", (field.source,)
            )
        return options
```

## 2. `src/curator/templates/partials/_detail_form_fields.html` (new file)

**Design note on `record[field.name]` vs. `record.get(field.name)`:**
using `.get()` explicitly rather than `[]` subscript, since `record` is
`{}` for a new record and every field must resolve to `None` cleanly
rather than risk a Jinja `Undefined` on a missing key.

```html
{#
  _detail_form_fields.html

  Renders the field inputs for a single entity's detail form — driven
  entirely by fieldkit's FieldDef list, no per-entity Jinja branching.
  Fetched by GET /panel/{entity}/{id} (or /panel/{entity}/new) and
  swapped into #detail-form-fields by detail-panel.js on every panel
  open. Replaces the old approach of one static per-entity form baked
  into _detail_panel.html at page load.

  Parameters:
    - fields  (list[FieldDef]) — from FieldKit.fields, in view column order
    - record  (dict) — current field values, or {} for a new record
    - options (dict) — source name -> list of {"value", "label"} dicts,
                        from FieldKit.options; only consulted for
                        field_type == "select"
#}
{% for field in fields %}
  <div class="form-group">
    <label for="detail-{{ field.name }}">{{ field.label }}</label>

    {% if field.field_type == "text" %}
      <input
        type="text"
        id="detail-{{ field.name }}"
        name="{{ field.name }}"
        value="{{ record.get(field.name) or '' }}"
        {% if field.placeholder %}placeholder="{{ field.placeholder }}"{% endif %}
      />

    {% elif field.field_type == "textarea" %}
      <textarea
        id="detail-{{ field.name }}"
        name="{{ field.name }}"
        {% if field.placeholder %}placeholder="{{ field.placeholder }}"{% endif %}
      >{{ record.get(field.name) or '' }}</textarea>

    {% elif field.field_type == "select" %}
      <select id="detail-{{ field.name }}" name="{{ field.name }}">
        <option value="">—</option>
        {% for opt in options.get(field.source, []) %}
          <option
            value="{{ opt.value }}"
            {% if record.get(field.name) == opt.value %}selected{% endif %}
          >
            {{ opt.label }}
          </option>
        {% endfor %}
      </select>

    {% elif field.field_type == "date" %}
      <input
        type="date"
        id="detail-{{ field.name }}"
        name="{{ field.name }}"
        value="{{ record.get(field.name) or '' }}"
      />

    {% elif field.field_type == "checkbox" %}
      <input
        type="checkbox"
        id="detail-{{ field.name }}"
        name="{{ field.name }}"
        {% if record.get(field.name) %}checked{% endif %}
      />
    {% endif %}

    {% if field.help_text %}
      <small class="form-help">{{ field.help_text }}</small>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
{% endfor %}
```

```python
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Options caching — select fields' options collected once, keyed by source
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestLoadOptions:
    """FieldKit.options caches get_lookup() results per source name, so
    the render step never needs its own DB call per request."""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_options_cached_by_source(self, tmp_path):
        db = _mock_db(
            [{"name": "type_id", "data_type": "bigint", "position": 1}],
            lookups={"project_types": [{"value": 1, "label": "Coding"}]},
        )
        overrides_path = _write_overrides(tmp_path, {
            "projects.v_project_detail": {
                "type_id": {"control": "select", "label": "Type", "source": "project_types"}
            }
        })

        kit = await FieldKit.create(db, "projects.v_project_detail", overrides_path)

        assert kit.options == {"project_types": [{"value": 1, "label": "Coding"}]}

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_shared_source_queried_once(self, tmp_path):
        """Two fields with the same source must only trigger one
        get_lookup() call — modeled here by two override entries
        pointing at the same source name."""
        call_count = {"n": 0}
        db = _mock_db(
            [
                {"name": "type_id", "data_type": "bigint", "position": 1},
                {"name": "other_id", "data_type": "bigint", "position": 2},
            ],
            lookups={"project_types": [{"value": 1, "label": "Coding"}]},
        )

        original_fetch_one = db.fetch_one

        async def _counting_fetch_one(sql, params):
            if "get_lookup" in sql:
                call_count["n"] += 1
            return await original_fetch_one(sql, params)

        db.fetch_one = _counting_fetch_one

        overrides_path = _write_overrides(tmp_path, {
            "projects.v_project_detail": {
                "type_id": {"control": "select", "label": "Type", "source": "project_types"},
                "other_id": {"control": "select", "label": "Other", "source": "project_types"},
            }
        })

        await FieldKit.create(db, "projects.v_project_detail", overrides_path)

        # _validate_sources calls get_lookup once per field (2 calls),
        # _load_options deduplicates by source (1 more call) -> 3 total,
        # not 4. This asserts the dedup in _load_options specifically,
        # not the (separately accepted) redundancy between the two
        # methods described in this changedoc's header.
        assert call_count["n"] == 3

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_no_source_fields_produce_empty_options(self, tmp_path):
        db = _mock_db([
            {"name": "name", "data_type": "character varying", "position": 1}
        ])
        overrides_path = _write_overrides(tmp_path, {})

        kit = await FieldKit.create(db, "projects.v_project_detail", overrides_path)

        assert kit.options == {}
```
