## 📄 vscode_cache_rant

# Gaslighting-as-a-Feature: The Feature That Saves You and the Bug That Gaslights You Are the Same Line of Code

*Notes from a debugging session, for whenever the dev.to post happens.*

## The symptom

Working through a series of markdown changedocs with Claude — each one
superseding the last as mistakes got caught and fixed. Same filename each
time, deliberately: `CHANGEDOC_WIRE_DETAIL_FETCH_TO_API.md`, deleted and
recreated on disk rather than renamed, to avoid a graveyard of
`_v2`/`_v3`/`_final_FINAL` files.

Third time downloading the revised file. Definitely not open in an editor
tab — closed it before the file was even replaced on disk. Opened it
again in VS Code.

It showed the **old** content. Not "slightly out of sync" old — showing
a version with a bug already confirmed fixed, with the corrected version
sitting right there in a browser tab for direct comparison.

## What it actually was

VS Code (like a lot of editors) caches file content by something more
persistent than "the path you typed" — plausibly the tab's file handle,
plausibly its own content cache, plausibly something in how it indexes a
delete-then-recreate at the same path. A plain edit-and-save is fine;
VS Code watches the file and reloads. A delete-and-recreate at an
identical path is apparently a different case, and not always one it
notices — even, per this session, when the tab was already closed before
the replacement happened.

## The part that makes it funny instead of just infuriating

This exact caching behavior is *also* the reason a crashed system doesn't
lose your open tabs — VS Code remembers what was open and restores it,
content and all, on next launch. That's genuinely good. That's the
feature working as intended.

It is, near as anyone can tell, **the same underlying mechanism** that
just spent several minutes making a fully sane person question whether
they were losing their mind. From the inside, "helpful crash recovery"
and "stubbornly gaslighting you about a file you definitely replaced" are
indistinguishable until you've already burned the time figuring out which
one you're looking at.

## The workaround

Close the whole editor. Not the file — the application. Reopen it fresh.

No amount of closing-and-reopening the tab, or the folder, or trusting
that "I definitely closed this before I touched the file" fixed it. Full
cold restart, every time a changedoc got revised under the same filename.

Renaming every revision (`_v2`, `_v3`) would dodge the bug, but trades a
five-second annoyance for a much worse one — a pile of near-identical
filenames with no clear "which one is current" answer, which is a worse
failure mode than the caching bug it avoids.

## The actual point, for anyone newer to a tool or a stack

For a few minutes, the instinct was "I must be doing something wrong" —
not "this tool is doing something wrong." That instinct isn't dumb, it's
just what happens when you don't yet have enough scar tissue with a
specific tool to instantly tell "I made an error" apart from "the tool
did something objectively unreasonable." Experienced users hit the exact
same VS Code behavior and think "ugh, cache, cold restart" in under a
second — not because they're smarter about it, but because they've
already spent the confusion budget on this specific bug once before and
filed it away.

When you're new to a stack, every friction point is ambiguous by
default. You don't have the backlog of "oh, THAT again" to draw on yet.
That ambiguity is the actual cost of being new — not a character flaw,
not a knowledge gap you're behind on. Just a rep count you haven't hit.

## Round two, which makes it worse, not better

Cold restart done. This time: open VS Code in an empty parent folder,
then navigate down into the actual project from inside the editor —
a different action entirely from "reopen the same directory." Should be
about as clean a slate as exists.

The changedoc tab was open again anyway.

This time the content was correct — the version downloaded three times
over, the one that actually matched disk. Which sounds like good news,
except it means the failure mode isn't "VS Code shows stale content,"
it's "VS Code will restore *some* tab state across an action that looks
nothing like session recovery, and whether what it shows you is right or
wrong is not something you can know in advance." A bug with a consistent
symptom is annoying but at least legible — you learn the pattern and
route around it. A bug that's sometimes silently correct is the one that
actually erodes trust, because now every open tab carries a "is this
real" tax, indefinitely, with no reliable signal for when to pay it.

## The tell, if you're stuck in that ambiguity right now

If a file's content looks wrong in a way that doesn't match what you just
did, and closing-the-tab/reopening-the-tab doesn't fix it — stop trusting
the editor specifically, not the file. Compare against a second source
(browser preview, `cat` in a terminal, anything that isn't the same
editor instance) before assuming you broke something. If the second
source agrees with what you expected and the editor doesn't, it's the
editor. Cold restart it and move on — it's not a reflection of anything
you did wrong.

---

*Working title candidates: "VS Code's Cache Doesn't Know the Difference
Between Saving Your Life and Ruining Your Morning" / "The Broligarchs'
Plot to Take Over the World By Driving Us All Mad, Episode 1: My Text
Editor"*

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_WIRE_DETAIL_FETCH_TO_API

# Changedoc: Wire `_fetch_*_for_display` to `api.get_*_detail()`

**Date:** 2026-07-01 (corrected)
**Correction note:** an earlier version of this changedoc used `...` to
skip repeating `_fetch_contacts`/`_fetch_organizations`, and silently
omitted `_resolve_type_status_names`/`_fetch_records`/the route handlers
from `projects.py`'s BEFORE/AFTER blocks entirely. That's a direct
violation of the "complete real code, never truncated" changedoc rule.
This version has full, untruncated file contents for all three route
files — confirmed against the `contacts.py` you just uploaded, which
matches what's below exactly.

**Reason:** Step 3 of the fetch-and-swap plan. `projects.py`/`contacts.py`/
`organizations.py`'s `_fetch_*_for_display` functions currently query
`projects.projects`/`identity.contacts`/`identity.organizations` directly
— the exact inconsistency `07_detail_views.sql`/`07_detail_api.sql` were
built to close. This changedoc is the Python side of that: the three
functions now call the `api.get_*_detail()` functions confirmed working
in pgAdmin.

**project_rules.md reviewed — no exceptions.** Single canonical
implementation (the view defines the shape once; Python no longer
duplicates it in a hand-written JOIN), tests included for the new
behavior.

**One real response-shape change, flagged rather than silent:**
`_fetch_project_for_display()`'s old direct query joined in `type`/
`status` *name* strings alongside `type_id`/`status_id`. `v_project_detail`
is a deliberate whitelist of editable fields only (see
`sql_conventions.md`) and doesn't include those joined names, and neither
`get_project()`'s JSON response nor `detail-panel.js`'s `populateForm()`
ever reads `record.type`/`record.status` — only the `_id` variants, plus
`name`/`description`. Also drops `slug` from the response — `slug` is
server-generated by `api.save_project()` and was never meant to be
directly editable, and nothing reads it either. Contacts and
organizations are unaffected: their old direct queries already returned
exactly `id`/`name`/`title`/`notes` and `id`/`name`/`notes` respectively,
matching `v_contact_detail`/`v_organization_detail` exactly.

**"Not found" changes representation, not behavior.** Before: a missing
record made `db.fetch_one()` return `None` directly. After: `fetch_one()`
always returns one row (it's a function call), whose single column is
`NULL` — so the *value* is still `None` once unwrapped, but the raw
`fetch_one()` return shape a test would need to mock is different
(`{"get_project_detail": None}` instead of bare `None`). The routes'
`if not record: raise HTTPException(404, ...)` checks don't change at
all — this is purely about what test mocks need to simulate.

## 1. `src/curator/web/deps.py`

**Why:** Both `call_proc()` (unwraps a `{success, data, message}`
envelope) and the new detail-fetch functions (unwrap a plain
record-or-`None`) need the identical mechanical step — pull the single
column value out of `fetch_one()`'s result, parse it if it came back as a
JSON string rather than an already-decoded dict. Factored into
`_fetch_json_scalar()`, with `call_proc()` now a thin wrapper over it.

### BEFORE (complete file)

```python
"""
curator.web.deps - FastAPI dependency injection.

Provides database connection and config manager as FastAPI
dependencies for use in route handlers. Also provides call_proc(),
a shared helper for unwrapping api.* stored-procedure JSONB envelopes —
used by every entity route module (projects.py, contacts.py,
organizations.py) that calls into the api schema.

The database connection is managed by dbkit, which reads connection
parameters from ~/.config/dev-utils/config.yaml under the 'dbkit:' key.
Passwords are handled by ~/.pgpass — no credentials in code or config.

Usage in routes:
    from curator.web.deps import get_db, get_config

    @router.get("/")
    async def my_route(
        db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
        config: ConfigManager = Depends(get_config),
    ):
        ...

Usage in middleware / non-route contexts (no Depends available):
    from curator.web.deps import get_db_direct

    db = await get_db_direct()
    result = await db.fetch_one(...)
    await db.__aexit__(None, None, None)
"""

import json
from typing import AsyncGenerator

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from fastapi import Depends

from curator.config import ConfigManager


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_config() -> ConfigManager:
    """
    Return a ConfigManager instance.

    A new instance is created per request. ConfigManager is lightweight
    — it reads from disk once at construction and caches in memory.
    """
    return ConfigManager()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Database — FastAPI dependency (use in route handlers)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def get_db(
    config: ConfigManager = Depends(get_config),  # pylint: disable=unused-argument
) -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncDBConnection, None]:
    """
    Yield an open AsyncDBConnection for the duration of a request.

    Opens a connection on entry, yields it to the route handler,
    then closes it on exit regardless of whether an exception occurred.

    dbkit reads connection parameters from:
        ~/.config/dev-utils/config.yaml  (host, port, dbname, user)
        ~/.pgpass                         (password)

    Yields:
        An open AsyncDBConnection.
    """
    async with AsyncDBConnection() as db:
        yield db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Database — direct async factory (use in middleware and auth routes)
# Middleware cannot use FastAPI's Depends() system, so this opens a
# connection directly. Caller is responsible for calling await db.__aexit__(None, None, None).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def get_db_direct() -> AsyncDBConnection:
    """
    Open and return an AsyncDBConnection without the FastAPI dependency system.

    Use this in middleware, background tasks, or any context where
    Depends() is not available. Always call await db.__aexit__(None, None, None) when done.

    Returns:
        An open AsyncDBConnection.
    """
    db = AsyncDBConnection()
    await db.__aenter__()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-dunder-call
    # Cannot use "async with" here — entry and exit are deliberately
    # decoupled by design. The caller (e.g. middleware.py) holds this
    # connection open across a wider scope than a single "with" block
    # could express, and is responsible for calling __aexit__() itself
    # once it's done. See module docstring's "Usage in middleware" section.
    return db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stored-procedure envelope helper
# Moved here from crew.py (2026-07-01 changedoc) — shared by every route
# module that calls an api.* proc. Not entity-specific, so it belongs in
# shared infrastructure rather than any one route file. Renamed from
# _call_proc to call_proc on the move: the leading underscore signaled
# "module-private," which stopped being true the moment a second module
# needed to import it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def call_proc(db: AsyncDBConnection, sql: str, params: tuple) -> dict:
    """Call a stored proc that returns a single JSONB envelope and unwrap it.

    Every api.* proc returns {"success": bool, "data": ..., "message": str}.
    fetch_one() gives back a dict keyed by the proc's column name (e.g.
    {"save_project": {...}}); this pulls out that single value and parses
    it if dbkit returned it as a JSON string rather than an already-decoded
    dict (encoding-dependent — see dbkit client_encoding note in handoff).

    Returns the envelope dict: {"success": ..., "data": ..., "message": ...}
    """
    result = await db.fetch_one(sql, params)
    envelope = list(result.values())[0]
    if isinstance(envelope, str):
        envelope = json.loads(envelope)
    return envelope
```

```python
Provides database connection and config manager as FastAPI
dependencies for use in route handlers. Also provides call_proc(),
a shared helper for unwrapping api.* stored-procedure JSONB envelopes —

The database connection is managed by dbkit, which reads connection

Usage in routes:

Usage in middleware / non-route contexts (no Depends available):

"""

import json
from typing import AsyncGenerator

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from fastapi import Depends

from curator.config import ConfigManager


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_config() -> ConfigManager:
    """
    Return a ConfigManager instance.

    A new instance is created per request. ConfigManager is lightweight
    — it reads from disk once at construction and caches in memory.
    """
    return ConfigManager()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Database — FastAPI dependency (use in route handlers)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def get_db(
    config: ConfigManager = Depends(get_config),  # pylint: disable=unused-argument
) -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncDBConnection, None]:
    """
    Yield an open AsyncDBConnection for the duration of a request.

    Opens a connection on entry, yields it to the route handler,
    then closes it on exit regardless of whether an exception occurred.

    dbkit reads connection parameters from:
        ~/.config/dev-utils/config.yaml  (host, port, dbname, user)
        ~/.pgpass                         (password)

    Yields:
        An open AsyncDBConnection.
    """
    async with AsyncDBConnection() as db:
        yield db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Database — direct async factory (use in middleware and auth routes)
# Middleware cannot use FastAPI's Depends() system, so this opens a
# connection directly. Caller is responsible for calling await db.__aexit__(None, None, None).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def get_db_direct() -> AsyncDBConnection:
    """
    Open and return an AsyncDBConnection without the FastAPI dependency system.

    Use this in middleware, background tasks, or any context where
    Depends() is not available. Always call await db.__aexit__(None, None, None) when done.

    Returns:
        An open AsyncDBConnection.
    """
    db = AsyncDBConnection()
    await db.__aenter__()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-dunder-call
    # Cannot use "async with" here — entry and exit are deliberately
    # decoupled by design. The caller (e.g. middleware.py) holds this
    # connection open across a wider scope than a single "with" block
    # could express, and is responsible for calling __aexit__() itself
    # once it's done. See module docstring's "Usage in middleware" section.
    return db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stored-procedure / detail-fetch envelope helpers
# Moved here from crew.py (2026-07-01 changedoc) — shared by every route
# module that calls an api.* function. Not entity-specific, so it belongs
# in shared infrastructure rather than any one route file.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def _fetch_json_scalar(db: AsyncDBConnection, sql: str, params: tuple):
    """Call a function/proc returning a single JSON(B) column and unwrap it.

    fetch_one() gives back a dict keyed by the function's column name
    (e.g. {"get_project_detail": {...}} or {"save_project": {...}});
    this pulls out that single value and parses it if dbkit returned it
    as a JSON string rather than an already-decoded dict
    (encoding-dependent — see dbkit client_encoding note in handoff).

    Returns whatever that single value is: a dict (proc envelope or
    detail record), or None if the column itself is NULL — e.g.
    api.get_project_detail() finding no matching row. Callers that
    always expect a value (call_proc, below) never see None in practice;
    callers that might get a miss (the detail-fetch functions in
    projects.py/contacts.py/organizations.py) check for it themselves.
    """
    result = await db.fetch_one(sql, params)
    value = list(result.values())[0]
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = json.loads(value)
    return value


async def call_proc(db: AsyncDBConnection, sql: str, params: tuple) -> dict:
    """Call a stored proc that returns a single JSONB envelope and unwrap it.

    Every api.* proc returns {"success": bool, "data": ..., "message": str}.
    Thin wrapper over _fetch_json_scalar — kept as its own name since
    "call a proc and get its envelope" reads more clearly at call sites
    than the more general _fetch_json_scalar would, even though the
    underlying mechanics are identical.

    Returns the envelope dict: {"success": ..., "data": ..., "message": ...}
    """
    return await _fetch_json_scalar(db, sql, params)
```

## 2. `src/curator/web/routes/projects.py`

**Why:** Replaces the direct JOIN in `_fetch_project_for_display` with a
call to `api.get_project_detail()`. Nothing else in the file changes —
`_resolve_type_status_names`, `_fetch_records`, and all four route
handlers are shown in full below for an accurate diff, even though only
the import line and one function actually differ.

### BEFORE (complete file)

```python
"""Project routes — CRUD for projects.projects via api.save_project /
api.delete_project.

Split out of crew.py's route monolith (2026-07-01 changedoc).
"""

import json

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db, call_proc

router = APIRouter()


async def _fetch_project_for_display(db: AsyncDBConnection, project_id: int) -> dict:
    """Fetch a project with joined type and status names for display.

    Returns dict with id, name, slug, description, type, status,
    type_id, status_id keys.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT
            p.id,
            p.name::text,
            p.slug::text,
            p.description::text,
            p.type_id,
            p.status_id,
            ps.name::text  AS status,
            pt.name::text  AS type
        FROM projects.projects p
        LEFT JOIN projects.project_status ps ON ps.id = p.status_id
        LEFT JOIN projects.project_type   pt ON pt.id = p.type_id
        WHERE p.id = %s
    """
    return await db.fetch_one(sql, (project_id,))


async def _resolve_type_status_names(
    db: AsyncDBConnection, type_id, status_id
) -> tuple:
    """Look up type and status name strings from their ids.

    api.save_project() takes name strings, not ids, so the browser's
    type_id/status_id selections are translated here before the proc call.
    Either id may be None; returns (type_name, status_name), each possibly
    None if not found or not provided.
    """
    type_name = None
    if type_id:
        row = await db.fetch_one(
            "SELECT name FROM projects.project_type WHERE id = %s", (type_id,)
        )
        type_name = row["name"] if row else None

    status_name = None
    if status_id:
        row = await db.fetch_one(
            "SELECT name FROM projects.project_status WHERE id = %s", (status_id,)
        )
        status_name = row["name"] if row else None

    return type_name, status_name


async def _fetch_records(db: AsyncDBConnection, role: str, search: str) -> list:
    """Fetch role-filtered projects, optionally filtered by search term.

    Returns list of dicts with id, name, type, type_id, status, status_id.
    """
    view_name = f"projects.{role}_view"

    if search:
        sql = f"""
            SELECT
                p.id,
                p.name::text,
                p.slug::text,
                p.description::text,
                ps.name::text  AS status,
                pt.name::text  AS type,
                p.type_id,
                p.status_id
            FROM {view_name} p
            LEFT JOIN projects.project_status ps ON ps.id = p.status_id
            LEFT JOIN projects.project_type   pt ON pt.id = p.type_id
            WHERE p.name ILIKE %s
            ORDER BY p.name
        """
        rows = await db.fetch_all(sql, (f"%{search}%",))
    else:
        sql = f"""
            SELECT
                p.id,
                p.name::text,
                p.slug::text,
                p.description::text,
                ps.name::text  AS status,
                pt.name::text  AS type,
                p.type_id,
                p.status_id
            FROM {view_name} p
            LEFT JOIN projects.project_status ps ON ps.id = p.status_id
            LEFT JOIN projects.project_type   pt ON pt.id = p.type_id
            ORDER BY p.name
        """
        rows = await db.fetch_all(sql)

    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


# -- Single project fetch (for detail panel) ----------------------------------

@router.get("/crew/projects/{project_id}")
async def get_project(
    project_id: int,
    db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Fetch a single project as JSON for the detail panel."""
    record = await _fetch_project_for_display(db, project_id)
    if not record:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Project not found")
    return JSONResponse(dict(record))


# -- Project save routes ------------------------------------------------------
# /crew/projects/save must be declared before /crew/projects/{project_id}/save
# to prevent "save" matching as a project_id integer.

@router.post("/crew/projects/save")
async def save_new_project(
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Insert a new project via api.save_project().

    Accepts JSON body: {name, type_id, status_id, description}
    Returns the new project record as JSON on success (200).
    Returns {"success": false, "message": "...", "data": ...} (200) on
    failure — e.g. missing name, duplicate name. The message is
    proc-supplied and safe to display directly in the UI. data is None
    for most failures but may carry extra context (e.g. conflicting_id
    on a duplicate-name rejection) for future UI features to consume.
    """
    body = await request.json()
    name = (body.get("name") or "").strip()
    type_id = body.get("type_id") or None
    status_id = body.get("status_id") or None
    description = body.get("description") or None

    if not name:
        return JSONResponse({"success": False, "message": "Name is required.", "data": None})

    type_name, status_name = await _resolve_type_status_names(db, type_id, status_id)

    user_id = request.state.user["user_id"] if request.state.user else None

    payload = {
        "name": name,
        "description": description,
        "type": type_name,
        "status": status_name,
    }

    envelope = await call_proc(
        db,
        "SELECT api.save_project(%s, %s)",
        (json.dumps(payload), user_id),
    )

    if not envelope.get("success"):
        return JSONResponse({
            "success": False,
            "message": envelope.get("message"),
            "data": envelope.get("data"),
        })

    new_id = envelope["data"]["id"]
    record = await _fetch_project_for_display(db, new_id)
    if not record:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Insert succeeded but fetch failed")

    return JSONResponse(dict(record))


@router.post("/crew/projects/{project_id}/save")
async def save_project(
    project_id: int,
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Save edits to an existing project via api.save_project().

    Accepts JSON body: {name, type_id, status_id, description}
    Returns the updated project record as JSON on success (200).
    Returns {"success": false, "message": "...", "data": ...} (200) on
    failure — e.g. missing name, duplicate name, project not found. data
    is None for most failures but may carry extra context (e.g.
    conflicting_id on a duplicate-name rejection) for future UI features
    to consume.
    """
    body = await request.json()
    name = (body.get("name") or "").strip()
    type_id = body.get("type_id") or None
    status_id = body.get("status_id") or None
    description = body.get("description") or None

    if not name:
        return JSONResponse({"success": False, "message": "Name is required.", "data": None})

    type_name, status_name = await _resolve_type_status_names(db, type_id, status_id)

    user_id = request.state.user["user_id"] if request.state.user else None

    payload = {
        "id": project_id,
        "name": name,
        "description": description,
        "type": type_name,
```

```python
"""Project routes — CRUD for projects.projects via api.save_project /
api.delete_project.

Split out of crew.py's route monolith (2026-07-01 changedoc).
"""

import json

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db, call_proc, _fetch_json_scalar

router = APIRouter()


async def _fetch_project_for_display(db: AsyncDBConnection, project_id: int) -> dict:
    """Fetch a project via api.get_project_detail() for the detail panel.

    Returns dict with id, name, description, type_id, status_id keys —
    the columns in projects.v_project_detail — or None if not found.

    No longer returns joined type/status *name* strings (the old direct
    query's `type`/`status` columns) or `slug`: v_project_detail is a
    whitelist of editable fields only. Nothing downstream reads those —
    detail-panel.js's populateForm() only maps name/type_id/status_id/
    description/title.
    """
    return await _fetch_json_scalar(
        db, "SELECT api.get_project_detail(%s)", (project_id,)
    )


async def _resolve_type_status_names(
    db: AsyncDBConnection, type_id, status_id
) -> tuple:
    """Look up type and status name strings from their ids.

    api.save_project() takes name strings, not ids, so the browser's
    type_id/status_id selections are translated here before the proc call.
    Either id may be None; returns (type_name, status_name), each possibly
    None if not found or not provided.
    """
    type_name = None
    if type_id:
        row = await db.fetch_one(
            "SELECT name FROM projects.project_type WHERE id = %s", (type_id,)
        )
        type_name = row["name"] if row else None

    status_name = None
    if status_id:
        row = await db.fetch_one(
            "SELECT name FROM projects.project_status WHERE id = %s", (status_id,)
        )
        status_name = row["name"] if row else None

    return type_name, status_name


async def _fetch_records(db: AsyncDBConnection, role: str, search: str) -> list:
    """Fetch role-filtered projects, optionally filtered by search term.

    Returns list of dicts with id, name, type, type_id, status, status_id.
    """
    view_name = f"projects.{role}_view"

    if search:
        sql = f"""
            SELECT
                p.id,
                p.name::text,
                p.slug::text,
                p.description::text,
                ps.name::text  AS status,
                pt.name::text  AS type,
                p.type_id,
                p.status_id
            FROM {view_name} p
            LEFT JOIN projects.project_status ps ON ps.id = p.status_id
            LEFT JOIN projects.project_type   pt ON pt.id = p.type_id
            WHERE p.name ILIKE %s
            ORDER BY p.name
        """
        rows = await db.fetch_all(sql, (f"%{search}%",))
    else:
        sql = f"""
            SELECT
                p.id,
                p.name::text,
                p.slug::text,
                p.description::text,
                ps.name::text  AS status,
                pt.name::text  AS type,
                p.type_id,
                p.status_id
            FROM {view_name} p
            LEFT JOIN projects.project_status ps ON ps.id = p.status_id
            LEFT JOIN projects.project_type   pt ON pt.id = p.type_id
            ORDER BY p.name
        """
        rows = await db.fetch_all(sql)

    return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    failure — e.g. missing name, duplicate name. The message is

    for most failures but may carry extra context (e.g. conflicting_id

        db,

            "data": envelope.get("data"),
```

```python
async def save_new_organization(
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Insert a new organization via api.save_organization().

    Accepts JSON body: {name, notes}
    Returns the new organization record as JSON on success (200).
    Returns {"success": false, "message": "...", "data": ...} (200) on
    failure — e.g. missing name, duplicate name.
    """
    body = await request.json()
    name = (body.get("name") or "").strip()
    notes = body.get("notes") or None

    if not name:
        return JSONResponse({"success": False, "message": "Name is required.", "data": None})

    user_id = request.state.user["user_id"] if request.state.user else None

    payload = {"name": name, "notes": notes}

    envelope = await call_proc(
        db,
        "SELECT api.save_organization(%s, %s)",
        (json.dumps(payload), user_id),
    )

    if not envelope.get("success"):
        return JSONResponse({
            "success": False,
            "message": envelope.get("message"),
            "data": envelope.get("data"),
        })

    new_id = envelope["data"]["id"]
    record = await _fetch_organization_for_display(db, new_id)
    if not record:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Insert succeeded but fetch failed")

    return JSONResponse(dict(record))

async def save_organization(

    user_id = request.state.user["user_id"] if request.state.user else None

    payload = {"id": organization_id, "name": name, "notes": notes}

    envelope = await call_proc(
        db,

    )

    if not envelope.get("success"):
        return JSONResponse({
            "success": False,
            "message": envelope.get("message"),
            "data": envelope.get("data"),
        })

    record = await _fetch_organization_for_display(db, organization_id)
    if not record:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Save succeeded but fetch failed")

@router.delete("/crew/organizations/{organization_id}")
async def delete_organization(

):
    """Delete an organization by id via api.delete_organization().

    Returns 204 No Content on success.
    Returns {"success": false, "message": "..."} (200) on failure —
    e.g. not found, or blocked by dependent records (foreign key violation).
    """
    user_id = request.state.user["user_id"] if request.state.user else None

    envelope = await call_proc(
        db,
        "SELECT api.delete_organization(%s, %s)",
        (organization_id, user_id),
    )

    if not envelope.get("success"):
        return JSONResponse({"success": False, "message": envelope.get("message")})
```

```python
"""Organization routes — CRUD for identity.organizations via
api.save_organization / api.delete_organization.

Split out of crew.py's route monolith (2026-07-01 changedoc).

import json

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db, call_proc, _fetch_json_scalar

router = APIRouter()


async def _fetch_organizations(db: AsyncDBConnection) -> list:
    """Fetch all organizations with their contact IDs.

    Returns list of dicts: id, name, contact_ids.
    contact_ids is a list of contact IDs belonging to this org.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT
            o.id,
            o.name::text,
            COALESCE(
                ARRAY_AGG(oc.contact_id) FILTER (WHERE oc.contact_id IS NOT NULL),
                '{}'
            ) AS contact_ids
        FROM identity.organizations o
        LEFT JOIN identity.organization_contacts oc ON oc.organization_id = o.id
        GROUP BY o.id, o.name
        ORDER BY o.name
    """
    rows = await db.fetch_all(sql)
    result = []
    for r in rows:
        d = dict(r)
        d["contact_ids"] = list(d["contact_ids"]) if d["contact_ids"] else []
        result.append(d)
    return result
```

```python
class TestFetchJsonScalar:
    """_fetch_json_scalar must handle a NULL column value (the
    api.get_*_detail() "not found" case) by returning None cleanly,
    not by crashing — this is new behavior TestCallProc never exercised,
    since every api.*() proc call_proc wraps always returns a non-null
    envelope.
    """

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_none_for_null_column(self):
        """Simulates api.get_project_detail(999999) — fetch_one() returns
        a row whose single column is None, and _fetch_json_scalar should
        pass that through as plain None, not attempt to unwrap or parse
        it further."""
        db = SimpleNamespace(
            fetch_one=AsyncMock(return_value={"get_project_detail": None})
        )

        result = await deps._fetch_json_scalar(
            db, "SELECT api.get_project_detail(%s)", (999999,)
        )

        assert result is None

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_dict_for_populated_column(self):
        """Simulates api.get_project_detail(23) finding a real row."""
        record = {"id": 23, "name": "Real Project", "description": None,
                  "type_id": None, "status_id": None}
        db = SimpleNamespace(
            fetch_one=AsyncMock(return_value={"get_project_detail": record})
        )

        result = await deps._fetch_json_scalar(
            db, "SELECT api.get_project_detail(%s)", (23,)
        )

        assert result == record
```

# Changedoc: Wire `_fetch_*_for_display` to `api.get_*_detail()`

**Date:** 2026-07-01 (corrected)
**Correction note:** an earlier version of this changedoc used `...` to
skip repeating `_fetch_contacts`/`_fetch_organizations`, and silently
omitted `_resolve_type_status_names`/`_fetch_records`/the route handlers
from `projects.py`'s BEFORE/AFTER blocks entirely. That's a direct
violation of the "complete real code, never truncated" changedoc rule.
This version has full, untruncated file contents for all three route
files — confirmed against the `contacts.py` you just uploaded, which
matches what's below exactly.

**Reason:** Step 3 of the fetch-and-swap plan. `projects.py`/`contacts.py`/
`organizations.py`'s `_fetch_*_for_display` functions currently query
`projects.projects`/`identity.contacts`/`identity.organizations` directly
— the exact inconsistency `07_detail_views.sql`/`07_detail_api.sql` were
built to close. This changedoc is the Python side of that: the three
functions now call the `api.get_*_detail()` functions confirmed working
in pgAdmin.

**project_rules.md reviewed — no exceptions.** Single canonical
implementation (the view defines the shape once; Python no longer
duplicates it in a hand-written JOIN), tests included for the new
behavior.

**One real response-shape change, flagged rather than silent:**
`_fetch_project_for_display()`'s old direct query joined in `type`/
`status` *name* strings alongside `type_id`/`status_id`. `v_project_detail`
is a deliberate whitelist of editable fields only (see
`sql_conventions.md`) and doesn't include those joined names, and neither
`get_project()`'s JSON response nor `detail-panel.js`'s `populateForm()`
ever reads `record.type`/`record.status` — only the `_id` variants, plus
`name`/`description`. Also drops `slug` from the response — `slug` is
server-generated by `api.save_project()` and was never meant to be
directly editable, and nothing reads it either. Contacts and
organizations are unaffected: their old direct queries already returned
exactly `id`/`name`/`title`/`notes` and `id`/`name`/`notes` respectively,
matching `v_contact_detail`/`v_organization_detail` exactly.

**"Not found" changes representation, not behavior.** Before: a missing
record made `db.fetch_one()` return `None` directly. After: `fetch_one()`
always returns one row (it's a function call), whose single column is
`NULL` — so the *value* is still `None` once unwrapped, but the raw
`fetch_one()` return shape a test would need to mock is different
(`{"get_project_detail": None}` instead of bare `None`). The routes'
`if not record: raise HTTPException(404, ...)` checks don't change at
all — this is purely about what test mocks need to simulate.

## 1. `src/curator/web/deps.py`

**Why:** Both `call_proc()` (unwraps a `{success, data, message}`
envelope) and the new detail-fetch functions (unwrap a plain
record-or-`None`) need the identical mechanical step — pull the single
column value out of `fetch_one()`'s result, parse it if it came back as a
JSON string rather than an already-decoded dict. Factored into
`_fetch_json_scalar()`, with `call_proc()` now a thin wrapper over it.

### BEFORE (complete file)

```python
"""
curator.web.deps - FastAPI dependency injection.

Provides database connection and config manager as FastAPI
dependencies for use in route handlers. Also provides call_proc(),
a shared helper for unwrapping api.* stored-procedure JSONB envelopes —
used by every entity route module (projects.py, contacts.py,
organizations.py) that calls into the api schema.

The database connection is managed by dbkit, which reads connection
parameters from ~/.config/dev-utils/config.yaml under the 'dbkit:' key.
Passwords are handled by ~/.pgpass — no credentials in code or config.

Usage in routes:
    from curator.web.deps import get_db, get_config

    @router.get("/")
    async def my_route(
        db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
        config: ConfigManager = Depends(get_config),
    ):
        ...

Usage in middleware / non-route contexts (no Depends available):
    from curator.web.deps import get_db_direct

    db = await get_db_direct()
    result = await db.fetch_one(...)
    await db.__aexit__(None, None, None)
"""

import json
from typing import AsyncGenerator

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from fastapi import Depends

from curator.config import ConfigManager


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_config() -> ConfigManager:
    """
    Return a ConfigManager instance.

    A new instance is created per request. ConfigManager is lightweight
    — it reads from disk once at construction and caches in memory.
    """
    return ConfigManager()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Database — FastAPI dependency (use in route handlers)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def get_db(
    config: ConfigManager = Depends(get_config),  # pylint: disable=unused-argument
) -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncDBConnection, None]:
    """
    Yield an open AsyncDBConnection for the duration of a request.

    Opens a connection on entry, yields it to the route handler,
    then closes it on exit regardless of whether an exception occurred.

    dbkit reads connection parameters from:
        ~/.config/dev-utils/config.yaml  (host, port, dbname, user)
        ~/.pgpass                         (password)

    Yields:
        An open AsyncDBConnection.
    """
    async with AsyncDBConnection() as db:
        yield db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Database — direct async factory (use in middleware and auth routes)
# Middleware cannot use FastAPI's Depends() system, so this opens a
# connection directly. Caller is responsible for calling await db.__aexit__(None, None, None).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def get_db_direct() -> AsyncDBConnection:
    """
    Open and return an AsyncDBConnection without the FastAPI dependency system.

    Use this in middleware, background tasks, or any context where
    Depends() is not available. Always call await db.__aexit__(None, None, None) when done.

    Returns:
        An open AsyncDBConnection.
    """
    db = AsyncDBConnection()
    await db.__aenter__()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-dunder-call
    # Cannot use "async with" here — entry and exit are deliberately
    # decoupled by design. The caller (e.g. middleware.py) holds this
    # connection open across a wider scope than a single "with" block
    # could express, and is responsible for calling __aexit__() itself
    # once it's done. See module docstring's "Usage in middleware" section.
    return db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stored-procedure envelope helper
# Moved here from crew.py (2026-07-01 changedoc) — shared by every route
# module that calls an api.* proc. Not entity-specific, so it belongs in
# shared infrastructure rather than any one route file. Renamed from
# _call_proc to call_proc on the move: the leading underscore signaled
# "module-private," which stopped being true the moment a second module
# needed to import it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Every api.* proc returns {"success": bool, "data": ..., "message": str}.
    fetch_one() gives back a dict keyed by the proc's column name (e.g.

    it if dbkit returned it as a JSON string rather than an already-decoded
    dict (encoding-dependent — see dbkit client_encoding note in handoff).
```

```python
"""
curator.web.deps - FastAPI dependency injection.

Provides database connection and config manager as FastAPI
dependencies for use in route handlers. Also provides call_proc(),
a shared helper for unwrapping api.* stored-procedure JSONB envelopes —
used by every entity route module (projects.py, contacts.py,
organizations.py) that calls into the api schema.

The database connection is managed by dbkit, which reads connection
parameters from ~/.config/dev-utils/config.yaml under the 'dbkit:' key.
Passwords are handled by ~/.pgpass — no credentials in code or config.

Usage in routes:
    from curator.web.deps import get_db, get_config

    @router.get("/")
    async def my_route(
        db: AsyncDBConnection = Depends(get_db),
        config: ConfigManager = Depends(get_config),
    ):
        ...

Usage in middleware / non-route contexts (no Depends available):
    from curator.web.deps import get_db_direct

    db = await get_db_direct()
    result = await db.fetch_one(...)
    await db.__aexit__(None, None, None)
"""

import json
from typing import AsyncGenerator

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from fastapi import Depends

from curator.config import ConfigManager


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_config() -> ConfigManager:
    """
    Return a ConfigManager instance.

    A new instance is created per request. ConfigManager is lightweight
    — it reads from disk once at construction and caches in memory.
    """
    return ConfigManager()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Database — FastAPI dependency (use in route handlers)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def get_db(
    config: ConfigManager = Depends(get_config),  # pylint: disable=unused-argument
) -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncDBConnection, None]:
    """
    Yield an open AsyncDBConnection for the duration of a request.

    Opens a connection on entry, yields it to the route handler,
    then closes it on exit regardless of whether an exception occurred.

    dbkit reads connection parameters from:
        ~/.config/dev-utils/config.yaml  (host, port, dbname, user)
        ~/.pgpass                         (password)

    Yields:
        An open AsyncDBConnection.
    """
    async with AsyncDBConnection() as db:
        yield db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Database — direct async factory (use in middleware and auth routes)
# Middleware cannot use FastAPI's Depends() system, so this opens a
# connection directly. Caller is responsible for calling await db.__aexit__(None, None, None).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def get_db_direct() -> AsyncDBConnection:
    """
    Open and return an AsyncDBConnection without the FastAPI dependency system.

    Use this in middleware, background tasks, or any context where
    Depends() is not available. Always call await db.__aexit__(None, None, None) when done.

    Returns:
        An open AsyncDBConnection.
    """
    db = AsyncDBConnection()
    await db.__aenter__()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-dunder-call
    # Cannot use "async with" here — entry and exit are deliberately
    # decoupled by design. The caller (e.g. middleware.py) holds this
    # connection open across a wider scope than a single "with" block
    # could express, and is responsible for calling __aexit__() itself
    # once it's done. See module docstring's "Usage in middleware" section.
    return db


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stored-procedure / detail-fetch envelope helpers
# Moved here from crew.py (2026-07-01 changedoc) — shared by every route
# module that calls an api.* function. Not entity-specific, so it belongs
# in shared infrastructure rather than any one route file.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def _fetch_json_scalar(db: AsyncDBConnection, sql: str, params: tuple):
    """Call a function/proc returning a single JSON(B) column and unwrap it.

    fetch_one() gives back a dict keyed by the function's column name
    (e.g. {"get_project_detail": {...}} or {"save_project": {...}});
    this pulls out that single value and parses it if dbkit returned it
    as a JSON string rather than an already-decoded dict
    (encoding-dependent — see dbkit client_encoding note in handoff).

    Returns whatever that single value is: a dict (proc envelope or
    detail record), or None if the column itself is NULL — e.g.
    api.get_project_detail() finding no matching row. Callers that
    always expect a value (call_proc, below) never see None in practice;
    callers that might get a miss (the detail-fetch functions in
    projects.py/contacts.py/organizations.py) check for it themselves.
    """
    result = await db.fetch_one(sql, params)
    value = list(result.values())[0]
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = json.loads(value)
    return value


async def call_proc(db: AsyncDBConnection, sql: str, params: tuple) -> dict:
    """Call a stored proc that returns a single JSONB envelope and unwrap it.

    Every api.* proc returns {"success": bool, "data": ..., "message": str}.
    Thin wrapper over _fetch_json_scalar — kept as its own name since
    "call a proc and get its envelope" reads more clearly at call sites
    than the more general _fetch_json_scalar would, even though the
    underlying mechanics are identical.

    Returns the envelope dict: {"success": ..., "data": ..., "message": ...}
    """
    return await _fetch_json_scalar(db, sql, params)
```

```python
    status_id = body.get("status_id") or None
```

```python
"""Contact routes — CRUD for identity.contacts via api.save_contact /
api.delete_contact.

Split out of crew.py's route monolith (2026-07-01 changedoc).
"""

import json

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db, call_proc

router = APIRouter()


async def _fetch_contacts(db: AsyncDBConnection) -> list:
    """Fetch all contacts with their first email address.

    Returns list of dicts: id, name, title, email, org_ids.
    org_ids is a list of organization IDs this contact belongs to.
    email is the first address from contact_emails, or None.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT
            c.id,
            c.name::text,
            c.title::text,
            (
                SELECT ce.address::text
                FROM identity.contact_emails ce
                WHERE ce.contact_id = c.id
                ORDER BY ce.id
                LIMIT 1
            ) AS email,
            COALESCE(
                ARRAY_AGG(oc.organization_id) FILTER (WHERE oc.organization_id IS NOT NULL),
                '{}'
            ) AS org_ids
        FROM identity.contacts c
        LEFT JOIN identity.organization_contacts oc ON oc.contact_id = c.id
        GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.title
        ORDER BY c.name
    """
    rows = await db.fetch_all(sql)
    result = []
    for r in rows:
        d = dict(r)
        # org_ids comes back as a PostgreSQL array — ensure it's a plain list
        d["org_ids"] = list(d["org_ids"]) if d["org_ids"] else []
        result.append(d)
    return result

            c.id,
            c.name::text,
            c.title::text,
            c.notes::text
        FROM identity.contacts c
        WHERE c.id = %s
    """
    return await db.fetch_one(sql, (contact_id,))
```

```python
"""Contact routes — CRUD for identity.contacts via api.save_contact /
api.delete_contact.

Split out of crew.py's route monolith (2026-07-01 changedoc).

import json

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response

from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db, call_proc, _fetch_json_scalar

router = APIRouter()


async def _fetch_contacts(db: AsyncDBConnection) -> list:
    """Fetch all contacts with their first email address.

    Returns list of dicts: id, name, title, email, org_ids.
    org_ids is a list of organization IDs this contact belongs to.
    email is the first address from contact_emails, or None.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT
            c.id,
            c.name::text,
            c.title::text,
            (
                SELECT ce.address::text
                FROM identity.contact_emails ce
                WHERE ce.contact_id = c.id
                ORDER BY ce.id
                LIMIT 1
            ) AS email,
            COALESCE(
                ARRAY_AGG(oc.organization_id) FILTER (WHERE oc.organization_id IS NOT NULL),
                '{}'
            ) AS org_ids
        FROM identity.contacts c
        LEFT JOIN identity.organization_contacts oc ON oc.contact_id = c.id
        GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.title
        ORDER BY c.name
    """
    rows = await db.fetch_all(sql)
    result = []
    for r in rows:
        d = dict(r)
        # org_ids comes back as a PostgreSQL array — ensure it's a plain list
        d["org_ids"] = list(d["org_ids"]) if d["org_ids"] else []
        result.append(d)
    return result


async def _fetch_contact_for_display(db: AsyncDBConnection, contact_id: int) -> dict:
```

### 5a. `tests/unit/test_deps.py` — add `TestFetchJsonScalar`

Add after the existing `TestCallProc` class. Uses `SimpleNamespace` and
`AsyncMock`, both already imported at the top of the file for `TestCallProc`
— no new imports required.

```python
class TestFetchJsonScalar:
    """_fetch_json_scalar must handle a NULL column value (the
    api.get_*_detail() "not found" case) by returning None cleanly,
    not by crashing — this is new behavior TestCallProc never exercised,
    since every api.*() proc call_proc wraps always returns a non-null
    envelope.
    """

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_none_for_null_column(self):
        """Simulates api.get_project_detail(999999) — fetch_one() returns
        a row whose single column is None, and _fetch_json_scalar should
        pass that through as plain None, not attempt to unwrap or parse
        it further."""
        db = SimpleNamespace(
            fetch_one=AsyncMock(return_value={"get_project_detail": None})
        )

        result = await deps._fetch_json_scalar(
            db, "SELECT api.get_project_detail(%s)", (999999,)
        )

        assert result is None

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_dict_for_populated_column(self):
        """Simulates api.get_project_detail(23) finding a real row."""
        record = {"id": 23, "name": "Real Project", "description": None,
                  "type_id": None, "status_id": None}
        db = SimpleNamespace(
            fetch_one=AsyncMock(return_value={"get_project_detail": record})
        )

        result = await deps._fetch_json_scalar(
            db, "SELECT api.get_project_detail(%s)", (23,)
        )

        assert result == record
```

```python
        db = SimpleNamespace(fetch_one=AsyncMock(side_effect=[
            {"save_project": save_envelope},
```

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_WIRE_DETAIL_FETCH_TO_API

# Changedoc: Wire `_fetch_*_for_display` to `api.get_*_detail()`

**Date:** 2026-07-01
**Reason:** Step 3 of the fetch-and-swap plan. `projects.py`/`contacts.py`/
`organizations.py`'s `_fetch_*_for_display` functions currently query
`projects.projects`/`identity.contacts`/`identity.organizations` directly
— the exact inconsistency `07_detail_views.sql`/`07_detail_api.sql` were
built to close. This changedoc is the Python side of that: the three
functions now call the `api.get_*_detail()` functions confirmed working
in pgAdmin.

**project_rules.md reviewed — no exceptions.** Single canonical
implementation (the view defines the shape once; Python no longer
duplicates it in a hand-written JOIN), tests included for the new
behavior.

**One real response-shape change, flagged rather than silent:**
`_fetch_project_for_display()`'s old direct query joined in `type`/
`status` *name* strings alongside `type_id`/`status_id`. `v_project_detail`
is a deliberate whitelist of editable fields only (see
`sql_conventions.md`) and doesn't include those joined names, and neither
`get_project()`'s JSON response nor `detail-panel.js`'s `populateForm()`
ever reads `record.type`/`record.status` — only the `_id` variants, plus
`name`/`description`. Confirmed by re-reading `populateForm()`: it maps
`name`, `type_id`, `status_id`, `description`, `title` and nothing else.
Also drops `slug` from the response — `slug` is server-generated by
`api.save_project()` and was never meant to be directly editable, and
nothing reads it either. Contacts and organizations are unaffected: their
old direct queries already returned exactly `id`/`name`/`title`/`notes`
and `id`/`name`/`notes` respectively, matching `v_contact_detail`/
`v_organization_detail` exactly.

**"Not found" changes representation, not behavior.** Before: a missing
record made `db.fetch_one()` return `None` directly. After: `fetch_one()`
always returns one row (it's a function call), whose single column is
`NULL` — so the *value* is still `None` once unwrapped, but the raw
`fetch_one()` return shape a test would need to mock is different
(`{"get_project_detail": None}` instead of bare `None`). The routes'
`if not record: raise HTTPException(404, ...)` checks don't change at
all — this is purely about what test mocks need to simulate.

---

## 1. `src/curator/web/deps.py`

**Why:** Both `call_proc()` (unwraps a `{success, data, message}`
envelope) and the new detail-fetch functions (unwrap a plain
record-or-`None`) need the identical mechanical step — pull the single
column value out of `fetch_one()`'s result, parse it if it came back as a
JSON string rather than an already-decoded dict. Factored into
`_fetch_json_scalar()`, with `call_proc()` now a thin wrapper over it,
rather than duplicating those three lines in four different places.

### BEFORE (the helper section — rest of the file unchanged)

```python
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stored-procedure envelope helper
# Moved here from crew.py (2026-07-01 changedoc) — shared by every route
# module that calls an api.* proc. Not entity-specific, so it belongs in
# shared infrastructure rather than any one route file. Renamed from
# _call_proc to call_proc on the move: the leading underscore signaled
# "module-private," which stopped being true the moment a second module
# needed to import it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def call_proc(db: AsyncDBConnection, sql: str, params: tuple) -> dict:
    """Call a stored proc that returns a single JSONB envelope and unwrap it.

    Every api.* proc returns {"success": bool, "data": ..., "message": str}.
    fetch_one() gives back a dict keyed by the proc's column name (e.g.
    {"save_project": {...}}); this pulls out that single value and parses
    it if dbkit returned it as a JSON string rather than an already-decoded
    dict (encoding-dependent — see dbkit client_encoding note in handoff).

    Returns the envelope dict: {"success": ..., "data": ..., "message": ...}
    """
    result = await db.fetch_one(sql, params)
    envelope = list(result.values())[0]
    if isinstance(envelope, str):
        envelope = json.loads(envelope)
    return envelope
```

### AFTER

```python
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stored-procedure / detail-fetch envelope helpers
# Moved here from crew.py (2026-07-01 changedoc) — shared by every route
# module that calls an api.* function. Not entity-specific, so it belongs
# in shared infrastructure rather than any one route file.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async def _fetch_json_scalar(db: AsyncDBConnection, sql: str, params: tuple):
    """Call a function/proc returning a single JSON(B) column and unwrap it.

    fetch_one() gives back a dict keyed by the function's column name
    (e.g. {"get_project_detail": {...}} or {"save_project": {...}});
    this pulls out that single value and parses it if dbkit returned it
    as a JSON string rather than an already-decoded dict
    (encoding-dependent — see dbkit client_encoding note in handoff).

    Returns whatever that single value is: a dict (proc envelope or
    detail record), or None if the column itself is NULL — e.g.
    api.get_project_detail() finding no matching row. Callers that
    always expect a value (call_proc, below) never see None in practice;
    callers that might get a miss (the detail-fetch functions in
    projects.py/contacts.py/organizations.py) check for it themselves.
    """
    result = await db.fetch_one(sql, params)
    value = list(result.values())[0]
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = json.loads(value)
    return value


async def call_proc(db: AsyncDBConnection, sql: str, params: tuple) -> dict:
    """Call a stored proc that returns a single JSONB envelope and unwrap it.

    Every api.* proc returns {"success": bool, "data": ..., "message": str}.
    Thin wrapper over _fetch_json_scalar — kept as its own name since
    "call a proc and get its envelope" reads more clearly at call sites
    than the more general _fetch_json_scalar would, even though the
    underlying mechanics are identical.

    Returns the envelope dict: {"success": ..., "data": ..., "message": ...}
    """
    return await _fetch_json_scalar(db, sql, params)
```

**Renamed rationale note applies as before** — `_fetch_json_scalar` stays
underscore-prefixed for now since, unlike `call_proc`, it's an
implementation detail import (three route modules import it, but it's
not itself the "public" operation being called — `call_proc` and the
`_fetch_*_for_display` functions are).

## 2. `src/curator/web/routes/projects.py`

**Why:** Replaces the direct JOIN with a call to `api.get_project_detail()`.

### BEFORE

```python
from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db, call_proc

router = APIRouter()


async def _fetch_project_for_display(db: AsyncDBConnection, project_id: int) -> dict:
    """Fetch a project with joined type and status names for display.

    Returns dict with id, name, slug, description, type, status,
    type_id, status_id keys.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT
            p.id,
            p.name::text,
            p.slug::text,
            p.description::text,
            p.type_id,
            p.status_id,
            ps.name::text  AS status,
            pt.name::text  AS type
        FROM projects.projects p
        LEFT JOIN projects.project_status ps ON ps.id = p.status_id
        LEFT JOIN projects.project_type   pt ON pt.id = p.type_id
        WHERE p.id = %s
    """
    return await db.fetch_one(sql, (project_id,))
```

### AFTER

```python
from dbkit.connection import AsyncDBConnection
from curator.web.deps import get_db, call_proc, _fetch_json_scalar

router = APIRouter()


async def _fetch_project_for_display(db: AsyncDBConnection, project_id: int) -> dict:
    """Fetch a project via api.get_project_detail() for the detail panel.

    Returns dict with id, name, description, type_id, status_id keys —
    the columns in projects.v_project_detail — or None if not found.

    No longer returns joined type/status *name* strings (the old direct
    query's `type`/`status` columns) or `slug`: v_project_detail is a
    whitelist of editable fields only. Nothing downstream reads those —
    detail-panel.js's populateForm() only maps name/type_id/status_id/
    description/title.
    """
    return await _fetch_json_scalar(
        db, "SELECT api.get_project_detail(%s)", (project_id,)
    )
```

## 5. Tests

Five existing tests need their `fetch_one` mock shape updated — not their
assertions, just what they simulate `fetch_one()` returning, per the
"not found changes representation, not behavior" note above. One new test
class added to `test_deps.py` for `_fetch_json_scalar`'s None-handling,
since that's genuinely new behavior `call_proc` never exercised.

### 5a. `tests/unit/test_deps.py` — add `TestFetchJsonScalar`

**Why:** `_fetch_json_scalar` returning `None` cleanly (rather than
crashing on `None.values()` or similar) is new, load-bearing behavior —
every detail-fetch function depends on it for the "not found" path. Add
after the existing `TestCallProc` class.

```python
class TestFetchJsonScalar:
    """_fetch_json_scalar must handle a NULL column value (the
    api.get_*_detail() "not found" case) by returning None cleanly,
    not by crashing — this is new behavior TestCallProc never exercised,
    since every api.*() proc call_proc wraps always returns a non-null
    envelope.
    """

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_none_for_null_column(self):
        """Simulates api.get_project_detail(999999) — fetch_one() returns
        a row whose single column is None, and _fetch_json_scalar should
        pass that through as plain None, not attempt to unwrap or parse
        it further."""
        db = SimpleNamespace(
            fetch_one=AsyncMock(return_value={"get_project_detail": None})
        )

        result = await deps._fetch_json_scalar(
            db, "SELECT api.get_project_detail(%s)", (999999,)
        )

        assert result is None

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_returns_dict_for_populated_column(self):
        """Simulates api.get_project_detail(23) finding a real row."""
        record = {"id": 23, "name": "Real Project", "description": None,
                  "type_id": None, "status_id": None}
        db = SimpleNamespace(
            fetch_one=AsyncMock(return_value={"get_project_detail": record})
        )

        result = await deps._fetch_json_scalar(
            db, "SELECT api.get_project_detail(%s)", (23,)
        )

        assert result == record
```

*(Needs `from types import SimpleNamespace` and `from unittest.mock import
AsyncMock` — both already imported at the top of `test_deps.py` for
`TestCallProc`, no new imports required.)*

## 📄 CHANGEDOC_DETAIL_VIEWS_AND_API_FUNCTIONS

# Changedoc: Detail views + `api.get_*_detail()` functions

**Date:** 2026-07-01
**Reason:** Step 2 of the fetch-and-swap detail-panel plan. Two things,
bundled because they're the same concern (the read path for the detail
panel) but kept SQL-only — no Python, no templates, no JS in this pass.

1. Closes the `web_app_user`/api-only inconsistency: `crew.py`'s (now
   `projects.py`/`contacts.py`/`organizations.py`'s) `_fetch_*_for_display`
   functions currently query `projects.projects` / `identity.contacts` /
   `identity.organizations` directly, which contradicts
   `06a_api_auth.sql`'s stated security model. New reads go through
   `api.get_*_detail()`, matching how writes already go through
   `api.save_*()`.
2. Gives the eventual field-schema system (`fieldkit`) something to
   introspect: `v_*_detail` views are a deliberate whitelist of exactly
   the columns each entity's detail form should show — see the new
   `sql_conventions.md` for the reasoning. Column order in each view is
   the field order the form will render in.

**Scope check against `project_rules.md`:** no hardcoded values, single
canonical implementation (Python doesn't duplicate what the view already
defines), database-first (verify in pgAdmin before any Python changes in
the next changedoc). No exceptions to flag.

**New numbered files, not edits to already-applied ones** — per the
convention just written down in `sql_conventions.md`.

---

## 1. `07_detail_views.sql` (new)

**Why these columns specifically:** each view is exactly the fields that
belong on that entity's detail form — `id` included (needed to know which
record you're looking at), `*_by` columns excluded (server-stamped, never
form fields), and for `projects.projects`, `slug` also excluded even
though nothing about its data type would otherwise flag it — it's
server-generated by `api.save_project()` and was never meant to be
directly editable. `notes` is included on contacts and organizations even
though the template doesn't render it yet (see the 2026-07-01 handoff's
"someday" list) — `api.save_contact()`/`api.save_organization()` already
accept it, so the view being ready now means the template gap is the only
remaining piece when that gets built.

```sql
-- =============================================================================
-- 07_detail_views.sql — Detail-panel-backing views
-- =============================================================================
--
-- One view per entity the detail panel can display: a deliberate
-- whitelist of exactly the columns that belong on that entity's
-- data-entry form. Not "the table minus a few exclusions" — id and *_by
-- columns are never included, and server-generated fields the user
-- shouldn't edit directly (e.g. projects.projects.slug) are left out
-- even though their data type wouldn't otherwise flag them.
--
-- Column order in each SELECT list is meaningful: it's the field order
-- the detail panel will render in once the field-schema system
-- introspects these views. Reordering a form's fields means reordering
-- the view here, not touching Python or template code.
--
-- See docs/sql_conventions.md for the full whitelist rationale.
--
-- Depends on: 02_identity.sql, 03_projects.sql
-- =============================================================================

CREATE VIEW projects.v_project_detail AS
SELECT
    id,
    name,
    description,
    type_id,
    status_id
FROM projects.projects;

CREATE VIEW identity.v_contact_detail AS
SELECT
    id,
    name,
    title,
    notes
FROM identity.contacts;

CREATE VIEW identity.v_organization_detail AS
SELECT
    id,
    name,
    notes
FROM identity.organizations;


-- =============================================================================
-- GRANTs
-- steward already has broader SELECT access to the underlying tables
-- (02_identity.sql, 03_projects.sql) — granting on these views too for
-- the same reason the role-filtered list views (captain_view etc.) are
-- granted: pgAdmin browsability without needing steward to know which
-- underlying table backs a view.
-- web_app_user gets nothing here — all access is through api.get_*_detail()
-- (07_detail_api.sql), consistent with the api-only read/write model.
-- =============================================================================

GRANT SELECT ON
    projects.v_project_detail
TO steward;

GRANT SELECT ON
    identity.v_contact_detail,
    identity.v_organization_detail
TO steward;
```

---

## 2. `07_detail_api.sql` (new)

**Why `LANGUAGE sql` instead of `plpgsql`:** each function is a single
`SELECT`, no branching or error handling needed — a not-found id just
returns `NULL`, same contract the old `_fetch_*_for_display` Python
functions already had (`db.fetch_one()` returning `None`), so the calling
route's `if not record: raise HTTPException(404, ...)` doesn't change.
`plpgsql`'s `DECLARE`/`BEGIN`/`EXCEPTION` scaffolding would be pure
overhead for a pass-through read.

```sql
-- =============================================================================
-- 07_detail_api.sql — API schema: get_*_detail() read functions
-- =============================================================================
--
-- Reads for the detail panel, routed through api.* the same way writes
-- already are — closes the gap where crew.py's old _fetch_*_for_display
-- functions queried projects.projects / identity.contacts /
-- identity.organizations directly, contradicting the api-only model
-- stated in 06a_api_auth.sql's header.
--
-- Each function returns the corresponding v_*_detail row as JSONB via
-- row_to_json(), or NULL if the id doesn't exist. Callers (Python routes)
-- check for None/null the same way they already do for the old direct
-- fetch functions — no change to error-handling shape.
--
-- Depends on: 07_detail_views.sql
-- GRANTs: web_app_user needs 06d_api_grants.sql re-run after this file —
-- the existing wildcard GRANT is a snapshot, it does not retroactively
-- cover functions created after it ran. See bottom of this file.
-- =============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION api.get_project_detail(p_id BIGINT)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE sql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
    SELECT row_to_json(t)::jsonb
    FROM projects.v_project_detail t
    WHERE t.id = p_id;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION api.get_contact_detail(p_id BIGINT)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE sql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
    SELECT row_to_json(t)::jsonb
    FROM identity.v_contact_detail t
    WHERE t.id = p_id;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION api.get_organization_detail(p_id BIGINT)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE sql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
    SELECT row_to_json(t)::jsonb
    FROM identity.v_organization_detail t
    WHERE t.id = p_id;
$$;


-- =============================================================================
-- GRANTs — re-run, don't skip
-- The wildcard grant in 06d_api_grants.sql only covered functions that
-- existed in the api schema at the moment it ran. These three are new,
-- so without re-running this, web_app_user can EXECUTE every other
-- api.* function but gets a permission error on these three specifically
-- — an easy thing to chase as a mysterious bug if this step is skipped.
-- =============================================================================

GRANT EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA api TO web_app_user;
GRANT EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA api TO steward;
```

---

## Apply order

1. Run `07_detail_views.sql` in pgAdmin against `wcyj`.
2. Verify each view directly: `SELECT * FROM projects.v_project_detail
   WHERE id = <some real id>;` (and the same for contacts/organizations)
   — confirms the whitelist looks right before any function wraps it.
3. Run `07_detail_api.sql` — includes the `06d` grant re-run at the

4. Verify grants landed: `SELECT grantee, routine_name FROM

5. Smoke-test each function directly in pgAdmin: `SELECT
   api.get_project_detail(<id>);` — confirm it returns the expected JSON

No Python changes in this pass — `projects.py`/`contacts.py`/
`organizations.py`'s `_fetch_*_for_display` functions keep querying the

is the next changedoc, once these are confirmed working from pgAdmin

## 📄 sql_conventions

# SQL Conventions — wcyj / steward repo

Living document. Add to it as new patterns get established; don't try to
anticipate every future case up front.

---

## Primary keys

- `BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY`, column named `id`.
- No exceptions across `audit`, `identity`, `projects`, `infrastructure`.

## Foreign keys

Two suffix conventions, and they mean different things to application code
— this distinction matters for anything (like `fieldkit`) that introspects
a table/view and needs to decide what to do with a column automatically:

- **`*_id`** — a real foreign key, always with a `REFERENCES` clause.
  User-facing (a project's `type_id`, a device's `node_id`, etc.). Any
  tool that auto-generates a form control from a column must treat every
  `*_id` column as "needs an explicit control declaration" — never
  default it to a plain number box. There are no bare, non-key
  integer/bigint columns anywhere in the current schema; if one is ever
  added (e.g. a quantity or integer-cents price for a future commerce
  schema), it should be treated the same way — explicit, not defaulted.

- **`*_by`** (`created_by`, `updated_by`) — also a `BIGINT` FK to
  `identity.app_user`, but server-stamped on save, never user-entered.
  These should not appear in any view meant to back a data-entry form —
  exclude them at the view layer, not by relying on downstream code to
  know to skip them.

- **`id`** itself — excluded from anything downstream the same way `*_by`
  is: it's identity, not a field a user fills in.

## Timestamps

- `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` on every mutable table.
- `updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`, maintained by the
  shared `public.set_updated_at()` trigger — never set manually in
  application code.

## Ordering

- No `sort_order` columns on lookup tables — `ORDER BY name` in queries.
  Stated in `01_audit.sql`'s header and followed consistently across
  `identity.*` and `projects.*` lookup tables.
- `projects.tasks.sort_order` is the one exception, and it's slated for
  removal (confirmed zero live call sites as of 2026-07-01) — manual
  task ordering is handled by naming convention instead (`01_first
  task`, `02_second task`, sorted by description) rather than a
  dedicated column.

## Views

- `v_` prefix for any view, e.g. `v_project_detail`.
- **Detail views** (`v_project_detail`, `v_contact_detail`,
  `v_organization_detail`, ...) are a deliberate whitelist of exactly the
  columns a data-entry form should expose — not "everything on the
  table minus a few exclusions." `id` and `*_by` columns are never
  included. Server-generated fields the user shouldn't edit directly
  (e.g. `projects.projects.slug`) are also left out, even though nothing
  about their data type would otherwise flag them for exclusion.
- Column order in a detail view's `SELECT` list is meaningful — it's the
  order fields render in on the form. Reordering a form's fields means
  reordering the view's `CREATE VIEW` statement, not touching Python or
  template code.
- Role-filtered list views (`captain_view`, `scribe_view`, etc.) are a
  separate, older pattern — `SELECT p.*` plus role-mapping joins — not
  subject to the whitelist rule above, since they're not form-backing.

## Read/write path through `api.*`

- `web_app_user` has `EXECUTE` on `api.*` only — no direct table or view
  grants. This was stated as the intended model from the start
  (`06a_api_auth.sql`'s header) but wasn't actually true in practice for
  a while (`crew.py`'s detail-panel fetch functions queried
  `projects.projects` etc. directly). As of the 2026-07-01 detail-panel
  work, reads go through `api.get_*_detail()` functions the same way
  writes go through `api.save_*()` — no exceptions, no "just this one
  read is fine to do directly" carve-outs.
- `api.get_*_detail(id)` functions return `JSONB` (via `row_to_json`),
  `NULL` if the id doesn't exist — same "let Python check for None and
  404" contract the old direct-query fetch functions used, so callers
  didn't need to change their error handling.
- Lookups (`project_types`, `project_statuses`, future ones) go through
  `api.get_lookup(name)` with explicit dispatch (`CASE`/`IF-ELSIF` on a
  known set of names) — not a generic `EXECUTE format('SELECT ... FROM
  %s', p_view_name)`. Dynamic SQL built from a caller-supplied identifier
  is avoided on principle even when the immediate source (a YAML file
  under your own control) isn't an attacker-controlled input.
- **New functions need `06d_api_grants.sql` re-run.** The wildcard
  `GRANT EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA api` is a snapshot at the
  time it executes, not a standing policy — it does not automatically
  cover functions created afterward. Any changedoc that adds new `api.*`
  functions must end with re-running the two `GRANT` lines from
  `06d_api_grants.sql`.

## Numbered migration files

- Already-applied files (`01`–`06d`) are not edited retroactively for
  new work — new schema changes get a new numbered file
  (`07_...`, `06e_...`) even if conceptually they'd sit naturally inside
  an earlier file. Keeps "what's actually been run against `wcyj`"
  unambiguous from the file list alone.
